_note: Admin changelog entries. Written by Claude from each commit's message, file list and size (git supplies the date, author and size). Add new entries at the top; the server inserts any new commit hash on boot and never overwrites an existing row. See docs/changelog.md.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare: version comparison subtitle instead of "Is it ready to submit?"
entries.goal: Stop the Verdict and review page asking "Is it ready to submit?" when two intentionally different versions are compared, where there is no verdict.
entries.whatChanged: The DocCompare app now says in its context message to the Vault page whether the results on screen are a version comparison (versions: true). The Vault page then shows a new subtitle for Verdict and review, "Version comparison: which sections are in both versions, worded differently or only in one, and any figures or quotes that differ." (VERSIONS_REVIEW_BLURB in docCompareTools.mjs); a normal check keeps "Is it ready to submit? Decide each change that matters, most serious first."
entries.benefit: The page heading matches what the screen shows: no submission question where there is no verdict.
entries.concerns: None known. Checked in the real local Vault (production build): versions mode shows the new subtitle, and a normal check afterwards shows the usual one; 219 app tests pass.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare addendum phase 6: intentionally different versions
entries.goal: Compare two versions that are meant to differ (a long and a short version, or versions for government and industry) without flagging every difference as a problem, while still catching a statistic or quote that changed between them (addendum §0.2).
entries.whatChanged: A "These are intentionally different versions" box in Compare documents, for one-off comparisons only (it switches off "Save this as your original?", as project rounds always use the full review). The drop zones become Version A and Version B and the same-document warning appears only below 30. New compare/sections.ts groups the sections of the two versions as in both, worded differently (with how alike; a renamed heading is matched by its text), only in A and only in B, returned as ComparisonResult.sections when the comparison is run in this mode. Verdict and review shows a new Version comparison view: no verdict and nothing to decide, the numbers and quotes that differ listed to check ("A figure differs in …"), and the grouped sections. The PDF report is titled Version comparison (sections table, numbers and quotes to check, then the full detail) with no verdict and no watermark, saved as version_comparison_….pdf, and the review for the author is not offered. Saved checks remember the mode and keep no verdict. Vault: a "Compare two versions meant to differ" job, a guide entry and (i) box text.
entries.benefit: Someone keeping an audience-specific version of a submission sees at a glance which sections were cut, added or reworded, and is still warned if a figure or quote no longer matches.
entries.concerns: Sections are matched by heading, then by text (renamed headings below 50% word overlap count as one only in A plus one only in B). Only number and quote changes are listed to check; an invented claim in version B shows only in All changes. The page around the app still shows the Verdict and review subtitle "Is it ready to submit?" in this mode. Checked with 219 app tests and in the real local Vault (production build and CSP: job card, Version A/B, project box off, grouped sections, figure listed, report title and file name, saved-check badge); not yet run on Railway.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare addendum phase 5: projects, rounds, timeline, export
entries.goal: Support the real workflow of reviewing a document several times: keep the original as a clean copy, check every later draft against it and against the previous draft, and show what was fixed, what is still missing and what is new (addendum §7, §8).
entries.whatChanged: New doc-compare/src/project/ modules. model.ts defines projects, rounds, stored files and tracked items, kept in a new IndexedDB store (database v3) with a memory fallback. accepted.ts builds the accepted state (the current original plus every accepted change, applied as edits by block id; derived, never stored; an accepted paragraph is held back while a red claim or quote in it is still open). track.ts gives each item a stable identity from where it sits in the original plus its kind, and works out its status in each round: new, open, not fixed ("You chose to restore this in round 2, but it's still missing", shown red), changed again, accepted (not asked again) or fixed, plus drift notes for items left from earlier rounds and the round summary ("Round 4: 3 issues fixed, 1 not fixed, 2 new changes."). engine.ts creates projects, adds rounds (each compared only with the accepted state and the previous round; the same file twice is refused), records decisions (undoing an acceptance in an earlier round re-checks the latest round), makes the latest round the new original (reason required, open red items listed and recorded as absorbed), deletes rounds (with every later round), compacts old rounds (files dropped, results kept; originals and the last two rounds keep their files), builds the timeline and the export reminder. transfer.ts exports and imports a project as one .doccompare zip. Every content change now carries its anchor in the original and the edit that applies it. UI: a Projects home screen (open, rename, export, import with Keep both / Replace, delete, storage warnings), a Timeline tool (rounds table with the biggest word loss marked, new original, delete, compact, export), project mode in Compare documents ("Save this as your original?" ticked by default; inside a project "Add the latest version" with a note), and on the verdict screen the project and round, the round summary, notes on cards, a Resolved list with Undo acceptance, and "This round only". The PDF report adds the round summary, a timeline table and every replacement of the original. Vault: Projects and Timeline tools, "Or open a project" on the start panel, a "Check a new draft of the same document" job, guide catalogue entries.
entries.benefit: After asking the LLM to "fix the issues", the person sees at once which fixes landed, which did not, and what else the LLM changed this time, without re-deciding changes they already accepted; the whole history can be exported and kept.
entries.concerns: Projects live in this browser only; clearing site data loses them unless exported. "Save this as your original?" is ticked by default, so the "Check a document" job now creates a project unless it is unticked (one-off checks still go to Saved checks). Only the latest round can become the new original. Accepting changes in the latest round does not re-check it; they shape the accepted state from the next round. Project settings cover word limit, page limit, required headings and protected terms only. Item identity across rounds relies on anchors in the original; a heavily restructured draft can show items as fixed and new rather than changed again (making the round the new original is the intended path). Checked with 215 app tests and in the real local Vault (production build and CSP: project created, round 2 summary and card notes, Resolved, This round only, duplicate file refused, timeline, export download, new original with reason, import Keep both); not yet run on Railway.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare addendum phase 4: references, citations, numbering, spelling, terms
entries.goal: Catch the reference, numbering and consistency damage an LLM edit causes: references and footnotes dropped, changed, renumbered or invented, citations left pointing at nothing or at the wrong source, numbering gaps, Australian spelling switched to US, and defined terms or acronyms lost (addendum §5.1, §5.3, §5.5).
entries.whatChanged: Readers now carry notes (DOCX footnotes.xml and endnotes.xml, Markdown [^n] footnotes and reference-link definitions, PDF footnotes found by best effort as small numbered text at the foot of a page), the notes each paragraph points to, and automatic list numbers (DOCX numbering.xml rendered as Word shows them; Markdown ordered lists). New checks in doc-compare/src/checks/: references.ts matches reference-list entries and notes between versions by fingerprint (Dice 0.85 on the text without its number and link) and reports removed, added (also counted as a claim) and changed (authors, year, title, link) as red, a renumbered list as amber, and citations ([3], [2-4], (Smith et al., 2021), Smith (2021), footnote marks) that point to nothing, now point to a different source, or were taken off or moved onto other text as red; reference-list paragraphs are no longer also compared as ordinary paragraphs, so a removed reference is one item. numbering.ts finds numbers from automatic numbering or the text (1., 2.3, (a), (iv), [3], Figure 2, Table 3) and reports gaps, repeats and steps back the original did not have, and paragraphs whose number changed (one grouped item), as amber; a paragraph whose only change is its leading number is no longer a red Number change. spelling.ts with spellingList.json (about 285 entries: -ise, -yse and -our stems expanded to their forms plus whole-word pairs; ambiguous words such as program/programme and licence/license left out) works out the original's standard and lists every switched word as a child of one amber item. terms.ts finds defined terms, acronyms with their expansion and capitalised phrases used 3+ times, plus Protected terms typed or loaded in Settings, and reports dropped or much less used terms, acronyms without their expansion and new unexplained acronyms as amber. File details gain References and Footnotes and endnotes rows; footnotes count in the word total (Settings). Review cards list the children of grouped items. Messages, verdict sentence, guide catalogue (glossary), (i) box and two new jobs (references and citations; spelling and terms); the structure job also shows numbering.
entries.benefit: A dropped or invented reference, a citation left pointing at the wrong source, a gap in the recommendation numbers or a switch to US spelling now shows on the verdict as a plain card, instead of being found by an assessor.
entries.concerns: PDF references and footnotes are best effort (footnotes must be in a smaller font at the foot of the page, with the mark in a smaller font too) and each PDF item says so. A Markdown reference link whose definition is missing is plain text to the parser, so it cannot be flagged. Term and acronym detection is pattern-based: an acronym defined in an unusual way may be reported as unexplained, and a section removal can also make terms used in it count as dropped. Removing a numbered heading or section now also reports the gap in the heading numbers (two test expectations changed). Checked with 201 app tests and in the real local Vault (production build and CSP: 16 jobs, reference and citation cards, File details references row, grouped spelling card with its word list, PDF best-effort note, a protected term card); not yet run on Railway.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare addendum phase 3: new claims, quotes, limits, headings, versions
entries.goal: Catch the submission problems an LLM edit causes beyond missing text: invented statistics, quotes and sources, reworded quotes, going over the word or page limit, missing or reordered required headings, and version numbers left unchanged (addendum §4, §5.2, §5.4, §5.6, §7.10).
entries.whatChanged: New modules in doc-compare/src/checks/, run in order by runPostChecks in compare/postChecks.ts (each sees what earlier checks found): claims.ts finds statistics (percentages, money, numbers with units, years after since/in/by…), citations ([3], (Smith et al., 2021), Smith (2021)), links and DOIs, sources ('a 2021 survey by the Housing Research Centre', 'according to …') and 4+-word quotes in added paragraphs and the inserted words of changed ones, and reports those not in the original as red New claim items (one per distinct claim); quotes.ts reports a direct quote that was reworded (with word diff) or removed as red, skipping quotes in wholly removed paragraphs; limits.ts reports going over a word limit (Compare screen and Settings) or page limit (Settings) as red and builds ComparisonResult.words (totals and per-section counts, reference list left out by default); headings.ts checks a pasted list of required headings (missing red, out of order amber; named templates saved in localStorage); version.ts finds 'Version 1.3', 'v1.3', 'Rev B', 'Draft 4' and version-history tables (not updated, changed without content change, removed or history not extended amber; backwards red). content.classify now treats a figure only inserted into a sentence as a new claim rather than a number change. Markdown block quotes are marked as quotes. UI: word limit box on Compare documents, Settings sections for limits and required headings with templates, Words by section table in File details, word totals on the verdict screen and report page 1. Messages, verdict sentence, guide catalogue (word-limit, word-counts, required-headings), (i) box and two new jobs (invented facts and quotes; within the word limit). Tests: tests/phase3.test.ts and fixtures uc03 required headings, uc04 invented claims and inserted statistic, uc05 quote changed, uc06 over word limit, uc11 version not updated and backwards; all earlier fixtures unchanged.
entries.benefit: An invented 67% or a made-up quote now stops the verdict at Not ready to submit with a plain card saying exactly what was added, and the word limit, required headings and version number are checked without reading the whole report.
entries.concerns: Claim detection is pattern-based: it can miss invented claims written in unusual ways (numbers in words, sources without capitals) and can flag a real number that is merely new to this draft; every new claim is red, so a deliberately added, correct statistic needs an Accept. A changed quote can also appear as a wording change on the same paragraph (two cards). Footnotes are not read yet, so the 'count footnotes' setting has no effect until phase 4. Version detection reads only the first 40 blocks or two pages. Checked with 155 app tests and in the real local Vault (production build and CSP: 14 jobs, new-claim and word-limit cards, totals line, words by section without the reference list, required headings with a saved template); not yet run on Railway.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare: labels and saved checks (search, open again, rename, delete)
entries.goal: Let the owner label a comparison, come back to it later, and find or delete past comparisons.
entries.whatChanged: Compare documents gains an optional Label box. Every successful comparison is saved in the browser's IndexedDB (src/review/savedChecks.ts; database doc-compare upgraded to v2 with a new 'checks' store, opened by the shared src/review/db.ts) with its label (or the edited file's name and the date), both files as Blobs, the file-pair key, and its latest verdict and decided count, kept in step as decisions change; comparing the same two files again updates the same saved check. New Saved checks tool (Compare group, and 'Or open a saved check' on the start panel; src/ui/SavedChecksView.tsx): newest first, search by label or file name (every word must match), Open (rebuilds the files and re-runs the comparison; decisions come back because they are keyed by the same file hashes), Rename, and Delete with an inline Delete? Yes / No that also removes the files and decisions. Starting a new check after a saved one clears the old label. Decision store gains remove(). App start() now takes the files explicitly (a saved check is opened and compared in one click). Wording that said 'nothing is saved' corrected in the guide, the (i) box and the privacy tooltip; guide catalogue gains saved and check-label; tour grows to 14 steps.
entries.benefit: Comparisons are no longer lost when the page closes: each one can be named, found by search, reopened with its decisions, renamed or deleted.
entries.concerns: Saved checks and their files live in this browser only: another browser or computer does not see them, clearing site data removes them, and a deleted check cannot be recovered (no recycle bin; export comes with projects in phase 5). Every comparison is saved automatically, so storage grows with use; the list shows sizes but there is no quota warning yet. Checked with 123 app tests and in the real local Vault (production build and CSP): labelled and unlabelled saves, verdict and decided count in the list, search, survival across a reload, reopening with decisions restored, rename, Delete with Yes / No, and upgrading a phase-2 v1 database without losing decisions. Not yet run on Railway.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare addendum phase 2: verdict, review queue, saved decisions
entries.goal: Turn DocCompare from 'show me the differences' into 'tell me if this is ready to submit, and make me deal with what isn't' (addendum §6 and part of §8).
entries.whatChanged: New Verdict and review tool (doc-compare/src/ui/ReviewView.tsx): a banner (Not ready to submit while a red item is open or marked Fix later; Review recommended while amber items are open; No significant changes found), a one-sentence summary built from the counts, the accuracy note, a decided counter, and a card per red and amber item with what happened, why it matters, the original and edited text and what to do. Red cards: Restore (copies the original text to the clipboard; file-detail cards just record), Accept, Fix later; amber cards: Accept and Dismiss all similar; Undo, Hide decided, Show in all changes, and R/A/L plus arrow-key shortcuts. Rules in src/review/verdict.ts (review items red then amber, stable item keys hashed from the change's content, verdict, progress, summary and decisions sentences). Decisions are stored in the browser's IndexedDB (src/review/decisions.ts, database doc-compare, store decisions) keyed by the SHA-256 of both files, with an in-memory fallback when storage is blocked. Vault's DocCompare page now opens with an 'Is it ready to submit?' panel and a Check a document button (new job 'check'); after comparing without a job the verdict opens. 'Changes' is renamed 'All changes'. The comparison report (pdfExport.buildReportPdf) starts with the verdict, summary, accuracy note and a decisions table, then 'Full detail'; while any red item is open every page carries an 'UNRESOLVED ISSUES - NOT READY TO SUBMIT' watermark. The review for the author leaves out accepted changes and says how many. Plain-language different-documents warning. Guide catalogue gains review, verdict and review-queue; tour grows to 13 steps (Settings text updated). Tests: tests/verdict.test.ts (queue order, stable keys, red/amber/green transitions, summary wording, no 'safe'/'correct'/'verified', decisions reload, report verdict page and watermark, author report excluding accepted).
entries.benefit: After comparing, the person sees one plain verdict and a short list of decisions instead of a long table, cannot get a clean report while a red item is open, and keeps their decisions across reloads.
entries.concerns: Decisions live in this browser only (IndexedDB): another browser or device, or clearing site data, starts again; projects with export arrive in phase 5. Decisions are keyed by the exact file bytes, so re-saving a file starts fresh, and a changed Settings value can change an item's wording and so its key. Restore only copies the original text; the person still pastes it back into their document. Checked with 118 app tests and in the real local Vault with the production build and CSP (start panel, verdict opening by itself, Restore copying to the clipboard, keyboard decisions, verdict transitions, decisions after a reload, Undo, report verdict page and watermark on every page, plain gate warning, 13-step tour); not yet run on Railway.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare addendum phase 1: tiers, plain-language messages, section drop
entries.goal: Lay the foundations for the submission-check addendum: every change explained in plain words with red/amber/info tiers, so the verdict screen and review queue (phase 2) have what they need.
entries.whatChanged: The Change type gains optional tier, summary, whyItMatters, action, decision, decidedAt and origin, and the addendum's new categories (newClaim, reference, citation, quote, numbering, wordLimit, spelling, terminology, requiredHeading, versionNumber, drift) join the union with labels and icons; nothing produces them yet. New doc-compare/src/report/messages.ts holds every plain-language summary, why-it-matters and action in Australian English; the pipeline annotates every change (pipeline.annotate) and the review for the author now prints 'Why it matters' under each action (actionFor moved into the catalogue). Re-tiering per addendum §3 in severity.ts: layout pixel changes and file-detail warnings drop from medium to low (info); a new red rule flags a section that lost more than 15% of its words, through a new post-processing stage, compare/postChecks.ts (sections under 40 words skipped; not raised where a removal or move in that section already explains it). The aligner pairs a paragraph cut down to a few of its own words as modified (word containment of at least 0.9) instead of removed plus added, so 'tightening' shows as content cut from that paragraph. Use-case fixtures on a new white-paper base: uc01 caveat dropped and section tightened, uc02 statistic changed, uc03 heading removed, uc07 table row lost, uc09 heading level; e2e tests also check every change is described and the red file-detail findings are exactly the expected ones. New tests/messages.test.ts (every situation worded, never 'safe', 'correct' or 'verified', Australian spelling, tiers, section drop, tightened pairing).
entries.benefit: Every finding now says in everyday words what happened, why it matters and what to do, and a section the LLM 'tightened' is flagged red even when no whole paragraph was removed.
entries.concerns: Results change on purpose: page layout differences and file-detail warnings (size, counts, dates) now show as Low instead of Medium, and fall out of the review for the author's list (only flagged High file details are kept). One test expectation changed (the removed-section instruction wording). The new pairing rule could pair two unrelated short paragraphs when one's words are nearly all inside the other; it needs 3+ words and 90% containment, and ranks below real matches. No visible screens changed yet; the verdict and review queue are phase 2. 107 app tests pass; not yet looked at in the deployed Vault.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare: audit against SPEC.md and the submission-check addendum
entries.goal: Do the audit the submission-check addendum requires before any work: what exists, how the code differs from SPEC.md, what each addendum section needs, and the decisions to take first.
entries.whatChanged: New doc-compare/docs/AUDIT.md: a map of the existing modules, seven differences between the code and SPEC.md (code wins, flagged: Settings is a view, the job dashboard, the embedded Vault font, extra severity rules, no MinHash, no PDF text-position or merged-cell comparison, the extra author review PDF), a table of what each addendum section needs with sizes and the modules it touches, five decisions with the owner's answers (keep the Vault shell and add a Check-a-document flow; projects in the browser's IndexedDB; restructures approved; re-tiering and spelling list as proposed), and six shippable phases.
entries.benefit: The addendum's large scope (several weeks) is broken into phases that each ship on their own, with the direction-changing decisions settled up front.
entries.concerns: Size estimates are judgement, not measured. The file was committed with the phase 1 'Done' note already in it, because phase 1 was finished in the same session and pushed together.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare: guided tour, Vault theme and font in the app, four more jobs
entries.goal: Give DocCompare a guided tour like Graphics, make the app inside the frame look exactly like the rest of Vault, and offer more jobs on its start screen.
entries.whatChanged: New client/src/utils/tours/docCompareTour.js: an 11-step Shepherd tour (welcome, jobs, tool list, Compare documents, the two checks, Changes, File details and PDF pages, the review for the author, Settings, the (i) and compass buttons, the guide). A tour cannot reach inside the frame, so a step about a tool switches the frame to that tool and points at the frame. Started from a compass button beside the title (ToolSidebar onTour), Settings -> DocCompare Tour (/doc-compare?tour=1, flag removed from the address), and the guide (new catalogue entry 'tour'). Its step counter writes into the step's own card; the shared pattern in the other Vault tours writes into the first card in the page, which is a hidden earlier card after step 1 (noted in docs/doc-compare.md, not changed there). New doc-compare/src/ui/theme.ts: when embedded, the app applies Vault's chosen theme colours and font from the same-origin vault-settings key and client/src/themes.js (as Route Tracer does) and follows changes from other tabs; buttons, inputs, chips and headings now use Vault's sizes and medium weight. Four more jobs on the start screen (check what the AI added, headings and structure, moved paragraphs, did the document shrink): 12 cards.
entries.benefit: New users get a two-minute walk through every part of DocCompare, the tool now looks like the rest of Vault in any theme, and there are more ready-made jobs to start from.
entries.concerns: Inside Vault the app now loads the chosen font from Google Fonts: a network request for the typeface only (never file data; Vault's own page already loads it), so the 'no network calls' rule now applies to the standalone build and to file handling, not to the embedded font. Checked in the real local Vault (production build and CSP): all 11 steps attached and switched the right tool, ?tour=1, completion remembered, 12 job cards, frame font, primary colour and button weight matched Vault, no page errors. Not yet run on Railway, and only the default Warm Sand theme was checked.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare: "Download review for the author" PDF
entries.goal: Give one button that produces a complete, actionable, formatted PDF to send back to whoever made the AI edit, so they can work through the fixes.
entries.whatChanged: New doc-compare/src/report/authorReport.ts builds review_<edited name>_<date>.pdf in the browser with jsPDF: a cover with the file names and a count box (Must fix / Please review / Minor), how to use the list, then every non-trivial change (whatever filters are set; trivial differences only counted, file details only when flagged Medium or High) grouped by severity. Each item has a tick box, number, change type and location, one plain instruction from actionFor() (for example restore the missing section, restore this text, check the changed figure "30" -> "60", confirm added text, review rewording, restore formatting), and the text: the word diff drawn word by word with removed words red and struck through and added words green and underlined, a missing section's contents listed once, a table row once, or the text once when only its place or formatting changed; footer with page n of N. Buttons: 'Download review for the author' at the top of the PDF report tool (a card with the counts) and on the Comparison done card. Arrows now print as -> in both PDFs (the built-in font is Latin-1). The guide catalogue gained 'author-report', the (i) box and tool tips describe it, and a new job 'Send the fixes back to the author' (Compare documents, then PDF report). Tests: tests/authorReport.test.ts (instructions per change kind, item order and filtering, and generated PDFs read back with pdf.js).
entries.benefit: One click gives the author a self-explanatory fix list (what is missing, which figures changed, what to restore), most serious first, instead of a raw comparison table.
entries.concerns: The PDF uses jsPDF's built-in Latin-1 font, so characters outside Western European languages print as ?. Very long paragraphs in the word diff stop after about 2,500 words, and a removed section lists at most 40 of its items. Checked with unit tests, a generated sample read back and looked at, and the buttons clicked in the standalone build; not yet clicked inside the deployed Vault.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare: Graphics-style page (tool list, job screen) and menu placement
entries.goal: Make DocCompare look and work like Graphics and Video Tools, and make it appear in the admin's saved menu instead of hiding in Unsorted.
entries.whatChanged: DocComparePage.jsx now uses the shared tool-page pieces: ToolSidebar with six tools in three groups (Compare documents; Changes, File details, PDF pages; PDF report, Settings), with a 'Compare two files first' / 'PDF files only' hint on tools that are not usable yet; the JobStart 'What do you want to do?' screen with seven jobs (check nothing was left out, numbers and dates, serious changes only, wording, formatting, PDFs page by page, report to share) from DOC_COMPARE_GOALS; BackToJobs and JobBar above each tool; ToolInfoModal for the (i) box; open-on-last-tool option. The app in the frame (doc-compare/src/ui/App.tsx) became one view per tool, switched by a new doc-compare:view message; the frame stays loaded so files and results survive switching and going back to the jobs. Job steps can preset the Changes filters, and a job moves on to its next step when Compare finishes. The app reports its view back (cause 'self' when it moved by itself, so the tool list follows). Filters moved into a useChangeFilters hook so the PDF report uses them; Settings is now a view, not a drawer; File details and PDF pages (page list with thumbnails) are full views; standalone builds show tabs. Menu: server/services/navSeed.js, run on boot from db.js, places each item in NEW_NAV_ITEMS (DocCompare, after Contract Review) into the saved nav_layout once and records it in workspace_settings nav_layout_seeded, so an admin who later moves it to the pool is not overruled; with no saved layout it only records. Guide catalogue (docCompareTutor.js) rewritten for the new tool and part ids; its test now also checks every job step names a real tool and a known filter.
entries.benefit: DocCompare is now in the menu next to Contract Review (and movable in the menu layout editor like any placed item), and it has the same job-led layout as the other tool pages: pick a job such as 'Check numbers and dates' and it opens the right tool with the right filter after comparing.
entries.concerns: navSeed writes the workspace's saved menu layout on the first boot after deploy (one-time, idempotent, recorded in nav_layout_seeded); verified with unit tests against a fake database, and on the local database only in the no-layout case, not against the production layout. The page was smoke-tested in the real local Vault (production build and CSP, 23 checks: menu entry, (i) box, tool list, hints, job flow with auto-advance and preset filter, views, report, results surviving, guide button), but the guide chat's answers were not tested with a real model and nothing was run on Railway yet. No tour, as before.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Build: skip onnxruntime CUDA download so the base image installs again
entries.goal: Fix the failed GitHub 'Base image' build so dependency changes reach the deployed image again.
entries.whatChanged: The base-image build of 83837499 failed at `npm install --include=dev`, the first fresh install since 2026-11-15 (earlier builds reused the cached layer). Reproduced on Linux Node 20 with only package.json and package-lock.json: onnxruntime-node (a dependency of @imgly/background-removal-node) downloads CUDA GPU binaries on install from the onnxruntime 1.17.3 GitHub release, and that asset now returns 404. Dockerfile.base now sets ENV npm_config_onnxruntime_node_install_cuda=skip before the install; the app image inherits it. With it the install succeeds and the CPU binaries (which background removal uses; there is no GPU) are present. Recorded in docs/deploy-speed.md under what has been done.
entries.benefit: Fresh base-image builds work again, so the DocCompare install layer and any later dependency change reach the deployed image instead of failing on GitHub.
entries.concerns: Verified by reproducing the root npm install in WSL on Linux Node 20 (fails without the setting with the same 404, passes with it), not yet by a GitHub base build; that runs on this push (10-15 minutes) and should be checked in the Actions tab. Background removal on the server was not re-run after the change; it never used the CUDA binaries. The base image still uses node:20-slim; Node 20 reached end of life in April 2026 and the workflow warns about Node 20 actions, which is a separate upgrade.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: DocCompare: compare an original document with its AI-edited version
entries.goal: Catch content an AI edit silently skipped or altered: compare an original document with the LLM-edited version and list every difference, without the files ever leaving the person's computer.
entries.whatChanged: New tool at /doc-compare (AI tools menu, flag docCompare, lifecycle preview). It is its own Vite + React + TypeScript app in vault/doc-compare/, built into dist/doc-compare-app/ by scripts/buildDocCompare.js (non-fatal) and framed by DocComparePage.jsx like Route Tracer. Readers for PDF (pdf.js, paragraphs from line spacing, headings from font size, paragraphs rejoined across page breaks), DOCX (straight from the XML with jszip + fast-xml-parser, styles and theme fonts resolved), Markdown (remark + GFM) and text. Gate 1 stops on different or unsupported types, legacy .doc, damaged, password-protected and scanned PDFs; Gate 2 scores how alike the files are (headings, 5-word overlap, structure) and warns below 60 with Cancel / Compare anyway. The comparison runs in a Web Worker: block alignment (LCS plus fuzzy pairing and moves), removed sections and table rows grouped, word diffs classed as number/date (High), typo or wording (High when a large part of a paragraph was dropped), formatting by character range, table shape, metadata flags (size, word-count drop, counts, dates, author). PDFs also get a page pixel diff (pixelmatch) and a side-by-side page viewer. Summary bar, filterable and sortable table with inline word diffs, settings drawer (thresholds, trivial whitespace/quote rules), and a downloadable PDF report (jsPDF). Help: a themed tooltip on every control (planner-core TooltipHost), the (i) How DocCompare works box (opens once), and a guide chat on guideCore/guideRouter (POST /api/doc-compare-tutor behind requireFeature and aiLimiter) whose Open buttons reach the app through postMessage; client/src/pages/docCompare/docCompareTools.mjs is shared by the app, host page and guide. doc-compare is installed in Dockerfile.base and added to the base-image workflow paths. Docs: docs/doc-compare.md, key-files.md, guide-chat.md.
entries.benefit: Missing paragraphs, dropped sections, changed numbers and quiet rewording in an AI edit are listed in seconds, with removed content shown first, instead of being found by reading both versions side by side. Nothing is uploaded or sent to a model, so it is safe for confidential documents.
entries.concerns: Slow deploy: package.json (build script) and Dockerfile.base changed, so GitHub rebuilds the base image (10-15 minutes); until it finishes, Railway's build installs doc-compare's packages itself (slower build, same result). Tested on generated fixture documents (77 tests in doc-compare/, an end-to-end test per fixture, a no-network test), a synthetic 200-page DOCX (under 1 s), and in a headless browser inside a Vault-like page with the production CSP (workers, tooltips, (i) box and every guide Open path passed). Not yet run on Railway, inside the real logged-in Vault, or on real AI edits; the guide chat's model answer was only tested with a fake model. Known limits: PDF report prints non-Latin-1 characters as ?, PDF text position and merged table cells are not compared, no tour and no microphone (speech recognition would send audio off the machine). The app bundle is about 2.6 MB (pdf.js and its worker inline).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Code Map: AI security review (layer 2)
entries.goal: Layer 2 of the security review: have the standard model read every route file for problems pattern checks cannot judge (one user reaching another's data, missing admin checks, injection, unsafe uploads, SSRF, leaked secrets), on request only.
entries.whatChanged: server/services/codeMap/aiReview.js is now kind-driven: KINDS.plainCode (the existing AI review, unchanged behaviour) and KINDS.security. The generic reviewFiles loop handles reuse by file hash, per-file failures and progress; reviewSites stays as a wrapper. The security kind finds every server/routes file except tests (173 files, ~52,000 lines), chunks them by 500 lines (about 230 calls on a first run), prompts with how the file is mounted (mountNote: public or behind sign-in, admin, feature flag, which export of a multi-router module) plus the file's first 40 lines for later chunks and Vault's auth/ownership/SQL/SSRF rules, and checks the JSON answer (line inside the chunk, known severity/category/confidence, code line taken from the file, max 20 per chunk). Usage logged as code_map_ai_security; high severity with high confidence raised in the inbox (codeMapAiSec:<file>:<hash>). Table code_map_ai_reviews gains kind (default plainCode); queries, trimming (last 10 per kind) and estimates are per kind; one AI review runs at a time across both kinds and a 409 carries runningKind. Estimate adds approxInputTokens. Routes take ?kind= (unknown kind is 400). Client: new useReviewJob hook (load, poll, resume, start; follows a 409 only for its own kind) now used by AiReviewView and the new AiSecurityReview section on the Security tab (inline confirm with calls and tokens, progress, severity filter, cards, Copy findings / Download CSV via aiSecurityMd / aiSecurityCsv). Guide catalogue, (i) box, docs/code-map.md and docs/key-files.md. Tests: aiReview.test.js grows to 11 (chunking, prompt and mount note, finding checks, security job and the shared slot), route test (kind pass-through), export test.
entries.benefit: A model-assisted security read of every route file, ranked by severity with line, fix and confidence, kept cheap on repeat runs, sharing one engine and table with the AI review instead of a copy.
entries.concerns: Never run against a real model or database: tested with fakes and a Vite build only; the first real run is roughly 230 model calls and ~630,000 tokens of code plus prompts, so check its cost in Usage. Findings are a model's reading of a 500-line part plus the file top: expect false positives and misses; it does not read the services a route calls, so checks done in helpers look missing (asked to mark those low confidence). The refactor touched the existing AI review (now the plainCode kind): its tests still pass, but the existing rows get kind plainCode by the column default, and the AI review tab now shows another kind's running review only as a message. Taking the shared slot means a long security review blocks the AI review tab until it ends. ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS kind runs on boot; not executed locally (Postgres down).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Code Map: live site security checks (layer 3)
entries.goal: Layer 3 of the security review: check what the running site actually does, not just the code, so a header removed by a config change or a route left open by a mount mistake shows up.
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/codeMap/liveCheck.js: runLiveChecks probes the site at getAppUrl(req) (APP_URL, never a typed address) with redirects off and 10-second timeouts: home page reachable, HTTP to HTTPS redirect, certificate days left (TLS connect), HSTS max-age, Content Security Policy (flags unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval in script-src), nosniff, framing (frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options), Referrer-Policy, no X-Powered-By, CORS answer to a foreign Origin on /api/health, up to 10 admin/authed GET routes without a :param from routeManifest.json refusing both a no-token and a made-up-token request, public GET routes answering without 5xx, and a broken JSON body POSTed to a non-existent path answered without a stack trace. Local http addresses mark HTTPS, certificate, HSTS and a missing CSP as not applicable. Route probes run in parallel (about 5 s against production). Service createLiveChecks stores results in new table code_map_live_checks (last 10), one run at a time (409), failing high checks raised in the inbox (codeMap:live:<id>). Routes POST /api/code-map/live-checks and GET /live-checks/latest (admin; manifest updated by hand). Security tab rewritten around a shared CheckCard: code checks as before, then a Live site section with Check the live site, last-run line and Copy live checks (liveMd; securityMd now shares checksMd). Guide catalogue (live-check entry), tab tip, (i) box, docs/code-map.md (request list, check table, what it cannot check) and docs/key-files.md. Tests: liveCheck.test.js (fake site, safe-request guarantees), route test (APP_URL used, body ignored), export test.
entries.benefit: A five-second, free check that the deployed site still sends its security headers, forces HTTPS, refuses anonymous API calls and does not leak errors, with failing high checks in the inbox.
entries.concerns: Run from a developer machine against production before commit: all 13 passed (certificate 36 days left). Not yet run from inside Railway (the server calls its own public address; should work, unverified), and the new table and routes were not run against a database (local Postgres down). Button only, so a regression is caught only when someone presses it; a weekly run was not added. It cannot test a signed-in non-admin against admin routes, routes with an id, write routes, or anything behind a sign-in. The 10 sampled protected routes are spread through the list, not all of them. In local development the error-leak check can fail because Express shows stacks outside production. The probes count against any general rate limit (about 30 requests per press).

entries.subject: Code Map: Security tab (layer 1, pattern checks on every run)
entries.goal: Give the owner a security review of the application inside Code Map. Layer 1 of the agreed plan: free pattern checks for common mistakes that run with every analysis, including the weekly one.

Checks: routes in the code missing from server/testing/routeManifest.json (routers taken off a module or built by a factory are skipped); public routes listed for review; request values pasted into SQL template strings (a fixed-text ternary allowed); route files with :param routes that never mention the user; secret-shaped values (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, GitHub, AWS, Slack, private keys; obviously fake test values skipped; matched values cut to six characters and never stored); eval / new Function and shell strings in files that load child_process; file paths from request values unless the same file tests the value against a pattern; dangerouslySetInnerHTML without a sanitizer in the file; sign-in routes in auth.js without a limiter (a route that only answers 403 is skipped); helmet / CSP / open CORS in server/index.js; and the tools' SSRF guard results gathered in one place. Result stored as security: { checks, counts }; new stage label in jobs.js; failing checks added to inboxItems (high only raised, once per check). New Security tab (SecurityView.jsx) with tiles and one card per check, gaps first, and Copy security (securityMd, also in the full-run Markdown download). Guide catalogue, (i) box, docs/code-map.md (check table with what each cannot see) and docs/key-files.md updated. Tests: security.test.js; jobs.test.js gains the security stage and an inbox test; export test extended.
entries.benefit: Every run now reports on common security mistakes at no cost, with file and line for each, high gaps reach the inbox, and the weekly run catches a new unlisted route, pasted SQL value or committed key without anyone asking.
entries.concerns: Pattern checks only: they miss a request value copied into a variable before reaching SQL, validation in another file, routers built by a factory (about 300 manifest routes cannot be matched, so only code-not-in-list is reported), and anything outside server/ and client/src/ (.env files are not scanned). The per-user check is file-level: a file that mentions the user once passes even if one query forgets it. First local run: no gaps, 2 to check (shared/token route files and two SVG dangerouslySetInnerHTML uses), 30 public routes; earlier false positives (a fake test key, a database exec, a validated projectId path, the closed /register route) were fixed in the checks, which could hide a real case of the same shape. Changes tab does not compare security between runs yet. Runs saved before this deploy show an empty Security tab until the analysis runs again. Not clicked through in a browser; tested by unit tests, a Vite build and a real local analysis.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Code Map: AI review - where plain code would beat a model call
entries.goal: Find places where Vault calls an AI model for work plain code (regex, parsing, lookups, rules) would do as well or better, so they can be made cheaper, faster and predictable. Run on demand only, as the owner asked (no cron).
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/codeMap/aiReview.js: finds model call sites in server/ by text search (callModel, messages.create/stream, generateContent; tests, comments and callModel.js left out; 113 sites in 65 files locally), tags each with its owning tool from the latest analysis run, and asks getModelsForUser().standard through callModel for a verdict per site (replace / hybrid / keep / unclear, confidence, what it does, why, alternative, saving), 4 sites per call with excerpts from explain.js gatherExcerpts. Answers are checked against the real lines; unknown lines and out-of-excerpt refs are dropped. Unchanged files (content hash + PROMPT_VERSION) reuse the last verdicts. Background job, one at a time, 3 files in parallel, progress polled; usage logged as code_map_ai_review with stored tokens and approximate cost; last 10 kept; high-confidence replace verdicts raised in the Suggestions inbox once per call site. New table code_map_ai_reviews with a one-running partial unique index and restart cleanup (server/db.js). Routes in server/routes/codeMap.js: GET /ai-reviews/estimate, POST /ai-reviews (aiLimiter), GET /ai-reviews, /latest, /:id; added to routeManifest.json as admin. New AI review tab (AiReviewView.jsx): last-run line, Run review with an inline confirm showing the number of model calls, verdict filter, one card per site, Copy review and Download CSV (aiReviewMd / aiReviewCsv in exportRun.mjs). Guide catalogue (codeMapTutor.js + codeMapTools.mjs), (i) box, docs/code-map.md and docs/key-files.md updated. Tests: aiReview.test.js (7), route test (+1), export test extended.
entries.benefit: A ranked, exportable list of model calls that could become plain code, with the reason and the alternative for each, refreshed cheaply because unchanged files cost nothing.
entries.concerns: Never run against a real model or database: tested with fakes (aiReview tests, route tests, guide tests, a Vite build), and the call-site search was run on the real code. The local Postgres was down, so the new table and SQL were not executed. The first real run is about 40 model calls (113 sites, 4 per call) on the standard model; check its cost in Usage. Verdicts are a model reading code excerpts, so they are advice; prompts built in another file will often come back unclear. Call sites made other ways (wrappers without callModel in the name) are missed. estimate reads every source file on the main thread (about half a second) each time the tab opens. routeManifest.json entries were added by hand, not with crossUser.test.js --update (needs the database). No compass tour step was added for the new tab.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Fix boot on an empty database: add ef_cases."clientId" after clients exists
entries.goal: Let Vault start on a brand-new, empty database (a new server, a restore into an empty database, a throwaway test database) without changing what existing databases have.
entries.whatChanged: server/db.js created ef_cases (Email Follow-Up) with "clientId" INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id) about 570 lines before the clients table, so on an empty database the main schema transaction failed with 'relation "clients" does not exist' and Vault exited. The column is no longer named in CREATE TABLE ef_cases; it is added with ALTER TABLE ef_cases ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "clientId" INTEGER REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE SET NULL right after clients is created, beside the existing plans clientId lines. On existing databases the CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is skipped as before and the ALTER is a no-op. New test server/db.freshSchema.test.js creates a throwaway database on this machine, loads db.js against it in a child process (waits for "[db] Schema ready" or "startup failed", 4-minute limit), checks the table count, the links to clients and that ef_cases.clientId still points at clients, boots again to prove the schema stays idempotent, then drops the database.
entries.benefit: A fresh database now builds all 259 tables on first boot, so test databases and a new or rebuilt server no longer need a copy of an old database to start. The new test catches the next table that points at one created later.
entries.concerns: Tested: the new test failed before the fix with the reported error and passes after it (first boot, schema checks, second boot). ef_cases on a fresh build was compared with the existing local database: same columns, types, NOT NULLs and constraint names (ef_cases_clientId_fkey, ON DELETE SET NULL); only the physical column position of "clientId" differs on new databases, and no code inserts into ef_cases by position. The local dev server restarted on the change and answers /api/health. Only this one ordering problem existed; nothing else in db.js was reordered. The test needs a local Postgres that can CREATE DATABASE and takes about a minute; there is no package.json script for it on purpose (fast deploys). Not tried on production, where the database already exists and the change is a no-op.

Brisbane time, update-not-duplicate, 401/400, CSV re-import, member 403, recycle-bin restore), cross-user (1516 routes), ownership and auth tests, and the page on the local app with real webhook posts and a CSV import, seen in screenshots at desktop and phone width. entries.subject: Web Extractor: load with a real browser, and sign in
entries.goal: Let the Web Extractor read pages that build themselves with JavaScript, and pages that need a username and password.

Usage is logged as changelog_ask; no model call is made when nothing matches. Each [hash] it was given becomes a link that opens and scrolls to that entry (clearing filters that hide it); hashes it was not given are left as text with a warning; 'Based on N updates' lists what was sent. aiLimiter added to the /api/changelog mount; the route file is now injectable and logs through getLogger. Entry selection is keyword rules, not search by meaning, so a question that names no date, area or file and shares few words with the entries falls back to the 40 newest, and the model is told when more matched than were sent. Each question is a paid call carrying up to 40 shortened entries (roughly 10-20K input tokens). aiLimiter on the mount also counts the page's one GET per load, which is harmless at 30 a minute.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Code Map: compare runs, Changes tab and weekly run (milestone 4)
entries.goal: Milestone 4 of the admin Code Map: show drift between runs, so a new gap or a falling score is noticed early, and run the analysis every week without anyone pressing the button.
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/codeMap/compare.js (pure) compares two stored run results. Findings are split into items: rule findings per tool (matched by rule id and tool id), cross-tool import cycles by their set of files, cron-requires-route by the cron file and the path it requires (so a moved line is not a change), housekeeping per backup or unused file. It returns new and resolved items (high first), items that moved between amber and red, per-tool score changes (biggest drop first), tools added or removed, all import cycles gained or lost, and summary deltas. GET /api/code-map/compare?from=&to= replaces the 501 (400 for bad ids or unfinished runs, 404 when a run is gone; the full results are not sent back). New server/cron/codeMapCron.js runs the analysis every Sunday at 03:17 Australia/Brisbane as the first admin inside withCronLock('codeMap'), waits for the run to finish, and skips the week if a run is already going; started in server/index.js with the jobs that run on every server. Found and fixed during that check: the run list did not refresh after a run finished. The weekly cron has not fired for real yet (first run Sunday 03:17 Brisbane after deploy); it runs on every server, including staging if staging has its own database, and puts its high findings in the first admin's inbox. Each weekly run counts towards the 30 kept runs. Changing a rule or renaming a tool or rule id shows up as drift (resolved and new at once). The compare reads two full results from the database (about 115 KB each) per request.

entries.goal: Milestone 2 of the admin Code Map: run the analysis as a background job, keep the results so runs can be compared later, serve them to the coming page, and raise high findings in the suggestions inbox.

New server/routes/codeMap.js at /api/code-map behind requireAdmin, no aiLimiter: POST /runs, GET /runs, /runs/latest, /runs/:id, and /compare answering 501 until milestone 4; the five routes are classed admin in server/testing/routeManifest.json. analyze() gained an onStage callback.
entries.benefit: An admin can start an analysis over the API and poll it; results are kept for comparison, and the high findings (AI routes without a rate limit, hardcoded model ids, a cron requiring route files) land in the inbox once, not again on every run.
entries.concerns: Nothing in the menu uses it until milestone 3, so it is reachable only through the API. The first run on the live site will put about 14 high items in the inbox of the admin who runs it (7 rate-limit, 4 model-id, 3 cron/route), from regex checks that can be wrong. Checked on the local database with the real app: a run took about 2 seconds, the health endpoint stayed responsive, the result is stored at about 113 KB, a second start got 409, a stale row was reset on restart, and a second run did not duplicate the inbox items; also passed crossUser, crossUserOwnership and auth tests. Not yet run on Railway. The worker thread's memory use on the live container is unmeasured. The fixed 'one run at a time' is per workspace, so two admins share it.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Code Map: analyzer service and tests (milestone 1)
entries.goal: Milestone 1 of the admin Code Map tool: a Node analyzer that reads Vault's own source and reports each tool's code, links, convention checks and ranked findings, replacing the Python prototype.
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/codeMap/, one module per stage: files.js (walk server/ and client/src/), imports.js (relative-import graph with index-file and lazy-import resolution), tools.js (tools from appNavigation.js plus Tasks and Chat, entry pages from App.jsx), mounts.js (app.use('/api/...') lines in server/index.js, including requireAnyFeature and router objects), ownership.js (mount owner table, reach, shared at 3+ tools, tool links), rules.js (the 14 checks as declarative entries with severity, why and fix), structure.js (iterative Tarjan cycles, largest files, fan-in, possibly unused files, backups, planner packages), findings.js (one finding per rule plus cron-requires-route, cross-tool cycles and housekeeping, sorted by severity then tools affected). index.js exports analyze({ root }); run.js prints a summary and writes the JSON. Tests: codeMap.test.js (27 cases on a fixture repo in __fixtures__/repo) and codeMap.accuracy.test.js (this repo against the prototype's sample-data.json). Nothing calls it yet: no route, table or page.
entries.benefit: Run with node, the analyzer matches the Python prototype exactly on this repo: 60 tools, 145 mounts, 11 cycles, 404 test files, and every tool's score, checks, owned files, tests and links are identical. It takes about 3 seconds, makes no model or network calls and adds no packages, so the deploy stays fast.
entries.concerns: Not wired into the app yet (milestone 2 adds the table, API and job). Regex-based like the prototype, so it inherits its false positives (for example the SSRF and model-resolver checks are heuristics). Planner package counts differ from the prototype on this machine because of local, git-ignored build folders (cellar-planner dist-lite and upload copies, shelf host/setup); in the container they should match. Git churn and hotspots are left out because the container has no .git. The accuracy test compares the repo without the analyzer's own folder; it will start failing as Vault's tools and mounts change, by design, and must then be read rather than tuned. Fixture files under __fixtures__/repo are copied into the container (about 60 tiny files) and are skipped by the analyzer.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Code Map kit: brief, prompts, Python reference
entries.goal: Keep the build kit for the planned admin Code Map tool in the repo, so each milestone session reads the same brief and the Node port can be checked against the Python reference.
entries.whatChanged: New folder specs/code-map/: the brief (code-map-brief.md), copy-paste prompts per milestone, a README, and reference/ with the Python analysis (analyze.py, slim.py), the prototype page and the sample data taken from commit 40bf883.
entries.benefit: The spec and its reference data are versioned with the code they describe.
entries.concerns: Docs only; nothing runs in the app. The folder is copied into the container by COPY . . (about 330 KB), which is harmless.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Cost tables: current Claude prices (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable, Haiku 5.5)
