entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML: alert when a web page is ready (toast anywhere in Vault + Needs attention)
entries.goal: The owner asked to be alerted when a background PDF → HTML page is ready, since they now leave the page while it works.
entries.whatChanged: New column pdf_html_jobs."seenAt": NULL from when a run starts until the finished page is opened in the tool (existing rows count as seen). New GET /api/pdf/to-html/jobs/alerts (running count + unopened finished runs). New client/src/components/PdfHtmlWatcher.jsx, mounted once in Layout beside Toast: checks once when Vault opens and every 15 s while a job started in this browser may be running (flag in client/src/pages/pdf/pdfHtmlWatch.js), then shows one toast per finished run ("... is ready as a web page. Open", or "did not finish" with See why); quiet while the tool is on screen. The dashboard Needs attention list gains "N web page(s) ready in PDF → HTML" until opened (routes/attention.js, services/attention.js + test). The tool reopens an unopened finished page first. Route manifest and docs updated.
entries.benefit: The owner hears when the web page is ready wherever they are in Vault, and the dashboard reminds them until they look at it.
entries.concerns: The toast relies on a flag in the browser that started the job; a job started on another device is announced when Vault next opens there (the one check on load) or via Needs attention, not live. Vault must be open in a tab for the toast; there is no email or desktop notification. Checked locally in a browser with a stand-in model: toast on the dashboard about 15 s after finishing, Needs attention item, clicking it opens the page, item and toast gone after opening.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML runs in the background with a progress bar; leave the page and come back
entries.goal: Sonnet gives much better pages but takes minutes. The owner asked for the work to run in the background with a progress bar, so the page can be left while it grows.
entries.whatChanged: New table pdf_html_jobs (one row per web page, kept 7 days) and server/services/pdfToHtmlJobs.js. Making a page and each change request are background jobs: POST /api/pdf/to-html/jobs answers at once; the tool checks GET /jobs/:id?light=1 every 2 seconds and shows the stage, a progress bar (3/8/12% while preparing, then 12–95% by characters written against an estimate, 100% when done), the characters written, and the page growing in the preview. Stop aborts the streamed model call (callModel gains onText and signal); a stopped change keeps the previous version. Hand edits and Undo are saved with the job (PUT /jobs/:id/html). Coming back to PDF → HTML reopens the running job or the last one opened; a list shows the last 10. One running job per person. On start-up db.js marks jobs cut off by a restart as stopped and deletes rows older than 7 days. The one-shot /to-html and /to-html/revise routes are removed; route manifest, guide wording, help and docs updated.
entries.benefit: Long, high-quality conversions no longer hit the gateway's five-minute limit or tie up the page; progress is visible and the result waits for the owner.
entries.concerns: PDF Tools stored nothing on the server before; this keeps each web page (with its pictures and page images, several MB) for 7 days in the database. A Vault deploy during a run stops that job (it says so; start again). The progress percentage is an estimate from the expected length. Nothing tells the owner the job finished while they are elsewhere in Vault; they see it when they come back. Checked locally in a browser with a stand-in streaming model and the local database: progress rising, leaving mid-run and coming back (bar picks up), finished page, change request, Stop, Undo kept after reload. Not run with a real model.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML: room for long pages (32k tokens, streamed), compact code, honest "ran out of room" message
entries.goal: The owner's one-page website mock-up failed on Haiku with "The web page was too long to finish in one go. Try fewer pages.": the answer hit the 16,000-token cap.
entries.whatChanged: PDF → HTML now allows 32,000 output tokens and 8 minutes. Claude answers are streamed through a new opt-in callModel option (stream: true, Anthropic only; uses messages.stream().finalMessage()), because the SDK refuses a non-streamed request above about 21,000 max_tokens; every other caller is unchanged. If a model reports a lower output limit ("max_tokens: 32000 > N") the call is retried once at N. The system prompt asks for compact code (no comments, shared classes, CSS variables for brand colours, one @media block per breakpoint). The out-of-room message names the model and how many tokens it wrote, and suggests trying again or another model instead of "fewer pages". Tests and docs updated.
entries.benefit: Long single pages such as website mock-ups can be finished in one answer, and the message no longer gives wrong advice.
entries.concerns: Not run against a real model (local keys invalid); the streamed request was checked to pass the SDK and reach Anthropic (it stopped at the invalid local key). A 32,000-token answer costs about twice the old maximum and can take several minutes, especially on Sonnet. Whether Railway keeps an HTTP request open for up to 8 minutes was not checked.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML: linked scrolling between original and preview; website job starts with PDF -> HTML
entries.goal: The owner asked for the original PDF and the preview to scroll together, and for the "Put a PDF page on a website" job to start with uploading the PDF rather than the rotate question.
entries.whatChanged: New Scroll linked / Scroll separately button (shown with the original and the Preview; on by default, remembered per browser as vault_pdf_html_link_scroll). Scrolling either side moves the other to the same share of the way down; an echo guard stops the two sides fighting. To do this the preview frame changed from sandbox="" to sandbox="allow-same-origin"; allow-scripts is still not given, so the built page cannot run anything, and cleanHtml still strips scripts and handlers. Job card steps swapped: 1. PDF → HTML, 2. Rotate Pages (only if the page came out sideways, then Continue with PDF → HTML). Docs and help updated.
entries.benefit: Comparing the design with the built page no longer needs two separate scroll bars, and the website job opens on the upload.
entries.concerns: Security trade-off accepted by the owner: allow-same-origin gives the preview Vault's origin. It stays safe only while allow-scripts is NOT added; the docs say so. Scrolling is proportional, so sections line up only roughly when the web page and the PDF have different proportions. The swapped job puts Rotate after the conversion, so a sideways page means converting twice. Checked locally in a browser with a stand-in model (50% -> 50%, 90% -> 90%, off stops it; job card order).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML: "Show original" puts the PDF page beside the preview or the code
entries.goal: Let the owner compare the built web page (or its code) with the original PDF without leaving the tool.
entries.whatChanged: New Show original / Hide original button in the PDF → HTML preview bar. When on, the panel splits: the original page(s) on the left (a whole-page picture the browser renders while converting; kept in memory, not sent to the server), and the Preview or the Code on the right. Side by side on wide screens (xl), stacked on narrower ones. On by default; the choice is remembered per browser (localStorage vault_pdf_html_show_original). Help text and docs updated.
entries.benefit: Mistakes in the built page are easy to spot against the design, and change requests can be written while looking at both.
entries.concerns: The two sides scroll separately: the preview frame is sandboxed without same-origin (so nothing in the built page can run or reach Vault), which also stops Vault reading its scroll position to keep them in step. Checked locally in a browser with the owner's PDF (split with Preview and Code, hide, remembered after reload) using a stand-in model.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML: read tall pages in slices, text in reading order, pictures as contact sheets, skip non-content layers
entries.goal: The owner's website mock-up (one 612 × 4535 pt page) came out badly: the model saw the page about 210 px wide, got the text out of order, missed most logos and used blank layers and a toolbar strip as pictures.
entries.whatChanged: Browser (new client/src/pages/pdf/pdfToHtmlLayout.mjs + test): a page taller than 1.6 × its width is cut into about 1400 px square slices top to bottom (40 px overlap, at most 14), each with its own text in reading order (items sorted by position into lines; a wide gap on one line kept apart with " │ "). Server (pdfToHtml.js): accepts slices with page/part labels; extracted pictures go to the model as 1024 px contact sheets of 16 on mid grey (white logos visible), each tile named in the prompt, within the 20-picture limit; pictures that are not content (plain one-colour layer, or a strip thinner than 24 px or 12 × longer than wide) are marked aiSkip, kept in the zip but not offered to the model, and the tool says so on hover. Prompt now says: layout, order and colours from the pictures, words from the text, no invented sections or menus, every logo in a logo grid, exact phone numbers and emails. Help text and docs updated.
entries.benefit: Long website mock-ups and similar tall pages reach the model readable and in order, with every logo and photo, so the page it builds can follow the design.
entries.concerns: Checked locally with the owner's PDF in a browser: 8 readable slices, text in page order, 31 pictures on 2 sheets, the 3 non-content pictures held back. The model's answer was NOT checked (local AI keys invalid), so the improvement in the built page is expected, not seen. Each request is larger (8 slices + 2 sheets, about 4.7 MB from the browser), so cost per conversion rises. Automatic still picks the first Claude model (Haiku in production); Sonnet is likely to do better on a page this size.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Extract Images: follow indirect colour spaces (palette logos and CMYK photos were skipped or left unconverted)
entries.goal: Stop Extract Images (and PDF → HTML, which uses it) skipping pictures whose colour space is stored as a reference to another object.
entries.whatChanged: rebuildRaster now reads /ColorSpace with lookup instead of get, so a palette (Indexed) picture whose colour space is an indirect reference is rebuilt as PNG instead of being skipped as "special colour format". The JPEG branch also follows the reference and treats a 4-channel ICC profile as CMYK, so those JPEGs are converted to RGB. On the owner's website mock-up PDF, 21 of 34 pictures (all the client logos) were skipped before; now all 34 come out. New test in pdfTools.test.js (fails without the fix).
entries.benefit: Logos and other palette pictures from design tools now come out of Extract Images and reach PDF → HTML.
entries.concerns: The CMYK-by-reference JPEG path is covered by reasoning only, not by its own test.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML: keep pictures within provider limits and show the model's real error
entries.goal: The owner's first live conversion (claude-haiku-4-5) failed with "The AI model could not be reached", which hid the real reason. Show the real reason, and make requests lighter like Graphics and Video Tools so they stay inside the providers' picture limits.
entries.whatChanged: Model errors now name the model and give the provider's own reason (providerReason/modelFailure): busy (529/503), rate limit (429), rejected key (401/403), unknown model (404), timeout, or the raw text. Still returned as 502 so a provider 401 cannot sign the person out; the server log line adds the picture count and prompt size. Page pictures are re-made on the server at 1568 px longest side as JPEG; extracted picture copies for the model are 512 px (was 768); at most 20 pictures go in one request (was up to 25), because Claude refuses pictures over 2000 px when a request has more than 20. Every extracted picture still goes in the zip. Test fixture PNG replaced: the hand-typed one was rejected now and then by libspng. Docs updated.
entries.benefit: If it still fails, the message says why; requests are smaller and avoid the many-pictures size limit.
entries.concerns: The real cause of the owner's failure is unknown: production logs were not available (Railway CLI not logged in) and the local AI keys are invalid. The picture limit is a likely cause for a picture-heavy page but is not confirmed. Not run against a real model.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF -> HTML: choose a model that can see pictures (Settings -> PDF Tools, automatic fallback)
entries.goal: PDF → HTML failed for the owner because the workspace default model is DeepSeek, which cannot look at pictures. Let the tool use a picture-capable model without changing the chat default.
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/pdfToHtmlModel.js: setting pdf_html_model (own, else first admin). Only connected text models that can see pictures are offered (same rule as callModel: not deepseek-, not ollama:). Empty = Automatic: the standard model if it can see pictures, else the first connected Claude model, else the first Gemini one. A stale choice falls back to Automatic. GET/POST /api/pdf/to-html/model-config. New Settings tab PDF Tools (AI and tools group, admin) with a model picker and a line explaining why Automatic picked what it did. The tool shows "Model: … (automatic: the default, …, cannot see pictures)" or "(chosen in Settings)" under the page range, and "Written by …" after converting. If nothing connected can see pictures it says to add a Claude or Gemini model. The four PDF → HTML routes were added to server/testing/routeManifest.json (missed in c6183f97). Settings nav test updated for the new tab; docs updated.
entries.benefit: PDF → HTML works with a DeepSeek default: it picks a connected Claude model automatically, and an admin can choose a specific one.
entries.concerns: Checked locally in a browser with DeepSeek as default (Automatic chose Claude; choosing Gemini in Settings switched the tool; reset worked), but the conversion ran against a stand-in model because the local AI keys are invalid. Production needs at least one Claude or Gemini model in Settings → AI & Chat; which ones are connected there was not checked. Cost depends on the picked model (Claude is dearer than DeepSeek). The crossUser route test was not run.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF Tools: correct PDF -> Word help, panel note, User Guide and docs (pdf2docx, not LibreOffice)
entries.goal: Make the PDF → Word wording match how it really works since commit e18fdb5c (pdf2docx), instead of saying LibreOffice.
entries.whatChanged: PDF → Word help box now says Word and OpenDocument are rebuilt with pdf2docx (real paragraphs, tables, pictures, a page per PDF page), browser-printed PDF fixes, plain text via LibreOffice. The panel note no longer blames LibreOffice and tells people to OCR scans first. The PDF Tools info box summary mentions PDF to HTML and drops "real LibreOffice conversion". User Guide splits Office → PDF (LibreOffice) from PDF → Word (pdf2docx). docs/pdf-agent.md endpoint row and error note corrected. The server error when neither converter is installed no longer says "coming soon".
entries.benefit: People see an accurate description of what PDF → Word does.
entries.concerns: Wording only; no behaviour change. Help box and panel note checked in a local browser.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF Tools: "Put a PDF page on a website" job card and User Guide entry for PDF -> HTML
entries.goal: Make the new PDF → HTML tool visible on the PDF Tools "What do you want to do?" screen, not only in the sidebar, and describe it in the User Guide.
entries.whatChanged: New job card "Put a PDF page on a website" (globe icon) with two steps: Rotate Pages (only if a page is sideways) then PDF → HTML. User Guide PDF Tools section gained a PDF → HTML line.
entries.benefit: The tool can be found from the PDF Tools start screen in plain words.
entries.concerns: The job card, its step 2 opening PDF → HTML and the /pdf?tool=pdftohtml link were checked locally in a browser; the conversion itself has still not been run against a real AI model (see the PDF → HTML entry).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF Tools: PDF -> HTML with picture extraction, preview, change requests and zip
entries.goal: Turn a PDF page (or up to 5 pages) into a responsive static web page that uses the pictures inside the PDF, let the owner preview it and ask for changes, and download it as a zip.
entries.whatChanged: New Convert tool PDF → HTML. The browser renders each chosen page (about 1400 px) and reads its text; POST /api/pdf/to-html copies only those pages into a small PDF, extracts their pictures with the existing Extract Images code (JPEG 2000 converted to PNG), names them image-01.jpg, image-02.png …, and sends the page pictures, up to 20 extracted pictures and the text to the standard-tier model with vision, which writes one HTML file with its CSS built in. Preview in a sandboxed iframe at Phone (390), Tablet (768) or Desktop width; Ask for a change (typed or spoken) calls /to-html/revise, which rewrites the whole page; Undo keeps 20 versions; Code view allows hand edits; Download zip (index.html + images/) is built in the browser. Model output is cleaned: scripts, frames, link/base tags, meta refresh, on* handlers and javascript: links removed. Provider errors are returned as 502, so a provider 401 cannot sign the person out. Registered in MODES, groups, tips, help and the PDF guide catalogue (HTML removed from its not-possible list); three icons added; this tool gets a 1700px panel. Logged as pdf_html / pdf_html_revise. Docs updated.
entries.benefit: A PDF flyer or page can become a phone-friendly web page with its images in minutes, refined in plain words, without hand-coding.
entries.concerns: Not verified with a real AI model: the local Claude and Gemini keys were invalid, so the browser flow (upload, convert, phone/tablet/desktop preview, change, undo, code view, zip) was checked locally with a stand-in model only; real output quality and timing are unproven until the first live run. Each convert or change is one standard-tier vision call (cost not measured; up to 16,000 output tokens, 4-minute timeout). Charts and logos drawn as vector lines are not extracted and become a labelled placeholder. Results are not stored; leaving the page loses them. A default model without vision (DeepSeek, Ollama) gets a clear error.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Live TV: TV guide, programme search, My shows, country typeahead, video stays in view
entries.goal: Add a TV guide to Live TV, let the owner search programmes and keep a list of favourite shows, make the country choice quicker to use, and keep the picture in view while scrolling the channel list.
entries.whatChanged: TV guide: the server reads the free i.mjh.nz guides (Australian free-to-air for one city, plus some streaming channels), matched to channels through iptv-org’s guides list, and stores the next 8 days in a new shared table live_tv_programmes. A new cron (liveTvGuideCron, every 6 hours, under withCronLock, skipped when nobody has favourites or plays) refreshes it; starring a channel with no guide yet triggers a refresh. Admins choose the city (workspace setting live_tv_guide_region); members see which is used. Under the picture, the chosen channel’s guide shows day buttons for a week, ON NOW and details; channel rows show what is on now. New Programmes tab searches titles, episode names and descriptions; new My shows tab lists starred programmes (new table live_tv_shows, followed by title) with every airing in the next week and Watch / Guide buttons. Country choice is now a typeahead picker: typing a name or code (AU, NZ, UK, US and some aliases) narrows the list and Enter picks the top one. The shared Combobox (also used by Measurements) gained keyboard typeahead and two optional settings (prefixFirst ranking, searchHint). Scrolling: the page no longer has its own non-scrolling scroll box, so on wide screens the Watch panel stays in view; on narrower screens and phones the same player frame moves into a draggable mini player (no reload) with Back and Stop. Guide chat catalogue, tour (now 6 steps), User Guide, docs and 8 new routes in the route manifest.
entries.benefit: See what is on and what is coming up without leaving Vault, find a show by name, and keep a personal list of shows with their times. Seen on the local app: a real guide refresh loaded about 3,000 programmes for 16 channels in about 8 seconds; ABC News showed ON NOW and 7 day buttons; a starred show appeared in My shows with 5 airings; searching “antiques” found it and Guide opened the right day. Typing “uk” put United Kingdom first, “new z” left only New Zealand, fast typing lost no keys, and the Measurements pickers still worked. At wide, medium and phone sizes the picture stayed visible after scrolling to the bottom of the list, without restarting. New guide tests, helper tests, guide chat test, cross-user tests (admin-only guide routes refuse members), guide registry and nav tests pass; client builds. No package.json change.
entries.concerns: Not run on Railway. A guide refresh briefly raises server memory (about 200 MB at peak locally while reading the guide files); watch it on Railway. One guide file (Flash) returns 404 at the source and is skipped. Most channels outside Australia have no guide. No reminders when a show starts. The shared Combobox change also affects every Measurements picker (checked locally, but only by a quick test). The mini player was not tried in Safari, and autoplay in a normal browser may start muted.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Live TV: free channels from the public iptv-org list, played by the browser
entries.goal: Let the owner watch free TV channels from around the world inside Vault, using the public iptv-org channel list, without Vault storing or relaying any video.
entries.whatChanged: New preview tool Live TV (/live-tv, Apps -> Personal, flag liveTv, off for members until an admin switches it on). The server downloads iptv-org’s channel, stream, blocklist, country and category files once a day (about 12 MB) and keeps a trimmed list in memory; adult channels, channels on the takedown/adult blocklist, closed channels and streams with no known channel are always left out. The page lists channels by All / Favourites / Recent, country (Australia first), kind and name (with a mic), and a tick box hides channels that cannot play in a browser. A channel plays in a separate player page shown in a frame (/api/live-tv-player/), which has its own security rules allowing outside video while the rest of Vault keeps its strict ones; it is served before login because it holds no data and only plays an address the page sends it. hls.js is saved in the repo (no package.json change). Each play result is recorded so links say whether they played last time; Open in VLC downloads a .m3u file (with the referrer/user-agent settings some links need) and Copy link copies the address. Favourites and play results are new tables (live_tv_favourites, live_tv_plays, trimmed to 300 per person). Guide chat, tour (Settings -> Tours), (i) box, User Guide entry, docs/live-tv.md; 9 routes added to the route manifest.
entries.benefit: Free-to-air TV from many countries in one place with favourites and a memory of which links work, at no bandwidth cost to Vault (the browser fetches the video). Seen on the local app: the Australian list loaded (40 channels that can play in a browser), 10 Bold played, star, Favourites/Recent tabs, search, the VLC file and phone width all worked with no page errors; a dead link and an unreachable host reported a plain reason within a second. New tests for the list (filtering, ordering, daily cache, failed refresh), the guide and the page helpers pass, as do the cross-user and ownership tests, guide registry and nav tests; client builds. No package.json change.
entries.concerns: Not run on Railway: the live security rules on the main page are stricter than local, and the player’s own rules were only seen working locally. The local browser test allowed sound on autoplay; in a normal browser a channel may start muted until the speaker is pressed. Not tried in Safari. Many links fail (off air, geo-blocked, or only playable on the broadcaster’s own site), so expect a third to a half not to play. The first visit after each restart waits 10-15 seconds while the list downloads, and the trimmed list adds some memory on the server. No logos (outside image hosts are blocked by Vault’s rules). Being on iptv-org’s list does not make a channel licensed in Australia; the help text says so. No TV guide yet.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Translate house styles: Download for review (Word) from Test this set
entries.goal: Let the owner hand a house-style test to a native speaker as a proper document to review, and make clear the AI version in a test is a check, not a suggested replacement.
entries.whatChanged: The Test this set window in House styles has a new button, Download for review (Word). It saves a Word document with a note for the reviewer, the guidance given to the translator, then for each example a table of the original, the approved translation and the AI version (made without seeing the approved one), tick boxes for which reads better (approved, AI version, both fine, neither) and space for comments, then overall comments and a "Reviewed by / Date" line. The reviewer can type into it, track changes or add comments and send it back. It is built in the browser with jszip, which was already installed. The test window now says plainly that the AI version is a check, not a suggestion, and the approved translation stays the standard. The guide and docs mention the button.
entries.benefit: A fluent reviewer gets a clear, printable, editable comparison to mark up, instead of a screen only the admin can see. Seen on the local app (stand-in translator): made a set, ran Test this set, pressed Download for review; the file downloaded and a Word-file reader (mammoth) read back every part, macrons included, with no page errors. A new test builds the document and reads it back each time. Guide and goals tests pass; client builds. No package.json change.
entries.concerns: The file has not been opened in Microsoft Word itself, only read back with a Word-file reader, which checks the content and structure but not exactly how Word lays it out (tick boxes use the ☐ character, which Word shows with a fallback font if Calibri lacks it). The AI versions in the local test were the stand-in's reversed words, not real Māori. The document holds the test as it was when downloaded; running the test again gives a new AI version, and with a real model it can differ slightly from run to run.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Translate: house styles per language (approved examples), one-word name protection
entries.goal: Let an admin give Translate approved examples of how a language should be written (for example idiomatic, elevated te reo Māori for corporate statements), because a real test with an approved English/Māori pair showed the translator going literal and drifting when told "informal".
entries.whatChanged: New screen House styles (admins only, under Wording). For any language that needs it, an admin makes sets: a name for the kind of content, a comment on how it is translated (register, re-expressing rather than word for word, names to keep), and examples of an original with its approved translation and an optional note. Sets apply to the whole workspace. On New translation, a House style list appears only for a language that has sets: Let Translate choose (the only set, or the closest one, asking the light AI model and falling back to shared words), a set by name, or No house style. The translator receives the comment and examples in full, shown in the direction of the job (into the language, or out of it); the checker gets a short note and lists clear departures starting "House style:". Saved wording from translation memory is not reused for such a job. Passes keep the house style and the result screen names it. Test this set translates each example's original with the set, leaving that example out so the translator cannot copy it, and shows the result beside the approved version. Deleted sets go to the recycle bin. Separately, one-word names on a keep-as-written list (capital first letter, three letters or more, such as "Taumata") are now locked the same way as multi-word phrases; lowercase single words are still left alone.
entries.benefit: Translations for languages that need a particular way of writing can follow examples approved by someone who knows the language, instead of the translator's literal default, and an admin can see before relying on it how Translate does against their own approved versions. Checked on the local app with a stand-in translator: 18 house-style checks (members can read but not change or test; each test hides its own answer; one set, two sets, a picked set and No house style choose correctly; the translator gets the comment and examples in full; saved wording skipped; other languages untouched; passes keep it; recycle bin round trip) pass, the earlier 41 draft and pass checks still pass, a browser run of making, testing, picking and seeing a set had no page errors, the cross-user tests pass in full (members get 403 on the four admin actions), and the translator, guide, recycle-bin and goals tests pass; client builds. No package.json change; the two new tables are created on start-up.
entries.concerns: No real AI has run with a house style: whether the real model actually matches the examples is the thing to check live (Test this set with the Taumata pair is the quickest way). "Let Translate choose" between several sets asks the light AI model; locally only the shared-words fallback ran. The examples ride on every part of a translation, so a set adds cost to every page translated with it (the screen caps what is sent at about 6000 characters and says when examples are left out). Test this set costs one translation per example, up to 10. A name written only in a set's comment ("Keep Taumata as written") is an instruction, not the strong lock; put it in Words to keep as they are or a glossary as well. The one-word name lock changes a rule kept deliberately since 2026-09-10 (no reason was recorded): a capitalised ordinary word put on a keep list is now frozen everywhere it appears. House styles are workspace-wide, so the ownership test now lists their two read routes as shared by design.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Route manifest: classify 15 routes added by earlier commits
entries.goal: Make the cross-user safety test pass again: it refuses to pass while any route the app serves is missing from the list of who may call it.
entries.whatChanged: Fifteen routes added by earlier commits were served but not listed in the route manifest: seven for AI Visibility (assistants, audits list, open, create, delete, markdown and PDF downloads), two for Graphics (expand, subject mask) and six for Video Tools (clean language and its text version, denoise, remove logo, remove silences, stabilise). They were added with the test's own update option, which classes a route by calling it signed out: all fifteen refused, so all are "signed-in only". The file's existing order was kept and nothing else in it changed.
entries.benefit: The test that checks no route leaks to signed-out callers, admin routes stay admin-only, and one person cannot reach another's data runs clean again, so a real new gap shows up instead of being lost among old ones. Run locally: all 1,466 routes listed, every non-public route answers 401 signed out, all 34 admin routes answer 403 to an ordinary member, and the ownership half passes.
entries.concerns: This only lists the routes; it does not change how they behave. The ownership half checks these routes the same way as every other route, but no extra test data was added for AI Visibility audits, so whether one person can open another's audit by id is only covered as far as the existing ownership probes reach. The test runs locally, not in the deploy.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Translate: drafts with passes and Keep, server-side PDF, several languages, keep time
entries.goal: Let the owner read a translation without downloading it, change it with more passes before anything is saved, translate one document into several languages at once, see pasted text after using it, choose how long translations are kept, and stop translations dying when the page is closed.
entries.whatChanged: A finished translation now waits as a draft, "Ready to read". Open result is a full screen with the original beside the translation part by part, the parts the checks are about marked, filters for all / marked / changed parts, and Copy translation. On a draft the person can add requirements (a rule in their own words, or a word to translate one way or keep as written; "Fix this word" fills one in from the checks), tick Remember on any to keep for future translations, and run another pass over the whole document or only the parts they tick. Every version stays readable under Version. Keep this version commits the version shown: only then are the PDF and Word/Excel files made, the wording added to translation memory and the learned glossary, and the remembered requirements saved (once, never twice). Reopen as a draft lets a kept translation be changed again. The PDF is now made on the server, so a translation carries on when the page is closed; the blocking progress window is gone, My translations shows live progress and a message with "Open it" says when one is ready. "Also translate into" makes several languages from one document at once, each with its own learned glossary. Pasted text shows as "Your pasted text" with Show text and Change text. My translations has "Translations are kept for" (90 days, 1 year, or until deleted). "Let me read it before it is kept" can be unticked to keep straight away (the quick-draft job does). New table translate_job_passes and column translate_jobs."updatedAt", both created on start-up. The browser PDF builder is removed. Guide, tour, (i) box, ready-made jobs (a new one for several languages), User Guide and docs updated.
entries.benefit: A translation can be read and corrected inside Vault before it is committed, closing the tab no longer loses work, and a document can go into several languages in one go. Checked on the local app with a stand-in translator that makes no paid calls: 41 server checks (draft, read, whole and partial passes, a second pass refused while one runs, Keep waiting for a pass, keeping an earlier version, PDF made on the server holding that version, translation memory and remembered requirements written only on Keep and not twice on a re-keep, reopen, three languages kept straight away each with its own glossary, recycle bin restoring all versions, another person refused, keep time) passed twice in a row; a browser run of paste, show and change text, two languages started without a blocking window, the ready notice, the result screen, a pass with a rule and a word, versions, Keep, PDF download, reopen and the keep-time choice saw no page errors, and the result screen fits a phone. Guide, goals, check report, fonts, recycle bin, cross-user ownership and nav tests pass; client builds. No package.json change.
entries.concerns: No real AI translation has been run with this code: the checks used a stand-in that reverses words, so whether the real model follows a written rule from a pass as reliably as a word requirement is unknown until tried live. Word and Excel files, Google Translate jobs and long documents were not run through Keep. Behaviour change: by default nothing is downloadable until Keep this version is pressed. A page left open from before this deploy that is watching a running translation will wait on its old progress window (the translation itself finishes and appears in My translations after a reload). A whole-document pass costs about as much as the first translation, so repeated passes multiply the cost. Translation memory is not used in a pass, so a pass of a long document is slower than a re-run of the same document would have been. Each version keeps a full copy of the translated text in the database until the translation is deleted. The keep-time clean-up only runs at start-up, and deletes for good without the recycle bin. Found, not fixed, not caused by this commit: the route inventory test still fails on 15 older routes missing from routeManifest.json.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Translate: recycle bin for deletes, reads off the AI limit, Settings tour, User Guide
entries.goal: Finish the items left over from the Translate page rework: make deletes recoverable, stop ordinary browsing of the page being refused as "Too many requests", list the tour in Settings, and bring the User Guide and docs up to date.
entries.whatChanged: Deleting a translation or a glossary now moves it to the shared recycle bin for 30 days and shows a toast with Undo; it can also be put back from Settings, Recycle bin. A translation is kept with its files (the original, the translated PDF and the Word or Excel copy). One that is too big for the bin (over about 40 MB with its files) is not deleted: the page says so and asks "Delete for good? Yes / No, keep it". A learned glossary that is restored after Translate has already started a new one for that language comes back as an ordinary glossary named "… (restored)". Reading in Translate (the lists, the status of a running job, the downloads) no longer counts against the limit of 30 AI requests a minute per person; starting a translation, the estimate, saving, deleting and emailing still count. Settings, Tours now lists "Translate Tour". The Translate section of the User Guide is rewritten to describe the page as it is now. The check report downloads, and is emailed, as check-report-<name>.txt to match its button. The Translate guide now says deletes go to the recycle bin, and docs/translate-agent.md no longer uses the old names or describes the removed confidence percentage.
entries.benefit: A translation or glossary deleted by mistake can be brought back for 30 days, and clicking around Translate is no longer refused for being too fast. Seen on the local app: deleting a translation and a glossary on the page, pressing Undo and both coming back; the Translate Tour button in Settings opening the page with the tour running; the new User Guide section; the check-report file name. Checked through the local server with made-up rows: a restored translation keeps its id, its check results and a PDF that is byte-for-byte the same; a restored glossary keeps its id and words; the learned-glossary case; a 35 MB translation refused by the bin, kept, then deleted only with the "for good" choice; another person's translation cannot be deleted; 70 list reads in a row all answered while saves were still stopped after 30. The recycle bin, guide, goals, check-report and cross-user ownership tests pass and the client builds. No package.json change.
entries.concerns: Not checked on the live app. The restore was tested with a tiny made-up PDF, not a real multi-megabyte translation with a Word or Excel copy; the 40 MB limit was tested only from the too-big side. Each deleted translation sits in the database with its files for 30 days, so heavy deleting uses space until then. No test file was added for the Translate recycle-bin adapter; the checks above were one-off scripts. All Translate reads are now unlimited: they are small reads of the person's own rows behind the login, but the translation memory download and file downloads could be called repeatedly by a script, and any GET route added to routes/translate.js later must not call an AI or paid service or it would be unlimited too. Deleting a translation that is still running leaves its background work going until its next checkpoint, as before. The 90-day automatic clean-up of old translations does not use the recycle bin. Found, not fixed, and not caused by this commit: the route inventory test (first half of npm run test:cross-user) fails because 15 routes from earlier commits (AI Visibility, Graphics expand and others) are not in routeManifest.json.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Translate: status check no longer counts against the AI rate limit
entries.goal: Stop a running translation from using up the person's whole allowance of AI requests, which got their other clicks on the Translate page refused with "Too many requests".
entries.whatChanged: While a translation runs, the page asks the server for its progress every 2 seconds. That is 30 requests a minute, exactly the shared limit of 30 AI requests a minute per person, so opening My translations, Glossaries or the guide during a run could be refused. The progress check (GET /api/translate/jobs/:id/status) only reads the person's own job and calls no paid service, so it no longer counts. A small wrapper, aiLimiterExcept, was added beside the AI limiter to leave named free requests out of the count; server/index.js uses it for Translate with a rule that matches only a GET to that exact address. Every other Translate request (starting a translation, the estimate, the lists, the downloads) is limited exactly as before. The note in docs/translate-agent.md is updated.
entries.benefit: During a translation the rest of the Translate page keeps working. Checked with real requests against the real limiter and the rule from server/index.js on a small stand-in app: 100 progress checks in a row were all let through, other requests were still stopped at the 31st in a minute, a progress check after that was still let through, and a POST to the same address or a look-alike address was still limited.
entries.concerns: Not checked on the full server or the live app: nobody has yet run a real translation and clicked around during it. The progress check now has no limit of its own; it is a small database read of the caller's own row behind the login, so the risk is low, but a script could call it as often as it likes. The other Translate reads (jobs list, glossaries, downloads) still count against the AI limit although they call no AI either; someone clicking through them quickly can still be refused.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Translate: job screen, My translations dashboard, plain-word result window, guide, tour
entries.goal: Make Translate work like the other tool pages (Style editor, PDF Tools, Graphics): start from what you want to do, find finished translations and their downloads easily, read the results in plain words, and have a guide and a tour.
entries.whatChanged: The Translate page is rebuilt. TranslatePage.jsx (2,600 lines) is now a small shell and the screens are separate files in client/src/pages/translate/. The page has a left-hand list of four screens: New translation, My translations, Glossaries and What it has learned. A "What do you want to do?" screen offers eight ready-made jobs (quick draft, document to send, compare with the original, Word or Excel kept editable, scanned PDF, te reo Māori, pasted text, a document type translated often); picking one fills in the options on New translation, and the form says so when Google Translate is not set up and Vault AI is used instead. My translations has count boxes (All, Ready, Need checking, Running, Did not finish), a search box and a one-line verdict on each finished job. The result window ("Open result") now has the downloads at the top, the verdict, then the list of what to look at in plain words, with the models, version and counts in a closed "Technical details (for support)" block; it also opens for a job with no saved check results. Lessons learnt and its list of everything applied are reworded in plain words (the stored labels are unchanged). Glossaries has New glossary, Open, an inline "Delete? Yes / No", and "Add from a CSV file". New screen "What it has learned" lists the applied rules and words and the stored wording per pair of languages, with "Download translation memory". Added: an (i) box, a 9-step tour (compass beside the title, or /translate?tour=1), a tooltip on every control, and the Translate guide (round button; POST /api/translate-tutor behind the translate switch and the AI rate limit; it sees no documents or translations). Three faults fixed on the way: Lessons learnt would not open (a missing import after the file split), the page broke when the jobs list request was refused or failed, and Open result did nothing for a job with no saved check results. Docs updated.
entries.benefit: Someone who is not technical can start a translation without working out the options, find a finished one and its downloads, and read what the checks found without jargon. Seen on screen on the local app with sample jobs: the job screen and its presets, My translations and its counts, the result window, the PDF and check-report downloads, Lessons learnt opening, creating, reopening and deleting a glossary (still there after a reload), What it has learned with its filter and the translation memory download, the (i) box, all 9 tour steps, the guide chat opening, and a phone-width screen with no sideways scroll. The guide, goals, check-report and guide-registry tests pass and the client builds. No package.json change, so the deploy is a fast one.
entries.concerns: A real translation was NOT run after the rework: the local app has no AI model, so starting a job, the progress window, the PDF being built in the browser at the end, the Word and Excel downloads and the cost estimate are untested in the new page. That code was moved between files, not rewritten, but it is the first thing to try. Also not pressed: Send in "Email these documents", "Apply selected" and "Always use this" in Lessons learnt, and asking the guide a question (its answers are untested; each question is a paid AI call). The tour and the result window were checked with made-up sample jobs, not real ones. Existing limit, not changed: every Translate request counts against the shared limit of 30 a minute per person and a running translation checks its status every 2 seconds, which uses all 30, so other clicks during a run can be refused with "Too many requests"; the page now keeps what it shows when that happens, but the new page makes a few more requests than the old one (the glossary list is read again each time Glossaries opens). Deleting a glossary or a translation is still permanent and does not go to the recycle bin. Older sections of docs/translate-agent.md still use the old names.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics jobs: reframe step in social, new QR code job, honest step-bar hint
entries.goal: Put the new AI fill and QR Code tool on the Graphics start screen ("What do you want to do?"), and stop the step bar telling people to use Use in… for tools that cannot receive a picture that way.
entries.whatChanged: "Post on social media" now starts with an optional Canvas Extend step (pad to square, 4:5 or 9:16, AI fill carries the scene on), then Text Overlay, Watermark, Export for Social. New ninth job "Make a QR code": QR Code, then Print Ready. The step bar's "when you are done" line now checks whether the next tool accepts Use in… (HANDOFF_MODES); when it does not (Print Ready, Smart Crop, Vectorize, Favicon and others) it says "download the result, then choose that file in …". This also corrects the existing print, product and logo jobs, which pointed at Use in… for tools that do not take it. The shared JobBar accepts carry as a function of the next tool; Video Tools, PDF Tools and CSS pass fixed text and are unchanged. The Ask Graphics "What it can actually run" box now mentions AI fill. goals test updated for the new step order; docs updated.
entries.benefit: People reach AI fill from the most-used job and get a QR code job without browsing the tool list, and the step bar no longer sends them to a Use in… option that does not exist. Seen on screen locally: the nine tiles, the social job opening on Canvas Extend, and the QR job's step bar with the download wording. goals, tool-count and tutor tests pass; client builds.
entries.concerns: The Canvas Extend step is optional but the bar still counts it ("Step 1 of 4"); someone with a photo already the right shape skips it via the step chips. Print Ready still cannot receive a picture through Use in…, so the QR job needs a download and re-open; adding Print Ready (and the other tools) as Use in… targets would remove that step. The changed JobBar is shared with Video Tools, PDF Tools and CSS: they pass plain text, which works as before, but their bars were not re-checked on screen.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Graphics: AI fill in Canvas Extend, one-click subject select, QR Code tool
entries.goal: Add three of the Canva-style gaps found in a review of Graphics: reframe a picture with AI-painted space instead of plain padding, select the main subject or background in one click instead of painting, and make QR codes inside Vault.
entries.whatChanged: Canvas Extend now fills the new space with Colour, See-through or AI fill, and has Pad to a shape buttons (1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 16:9, 1.91:1, 3:2). AI fill (POST /api/graphics/expand) sends a shrunk copy with a blurred-mirror guide and a mask (new space plus a 16px seam) to the same FAL inpaint model as Inpaint, then lays the original back on top at full resolution with a soft edge, so only the new space is AI. Limits: FAL provider only, at most twice the width and height added, 40 MP, JPEG out. Inpaint, Eraser and Extract Element gain Subject / Background buttons (POST /api/graphics/subject-mask, the Background cut-out returned as a soft mask, applied like a magic-wand selection, cached per picture). New QR Code tool in Compose: link, text, Wi-Fi, email, phone, text message, contact card; colours with Brand Kit swatches, see-through background, size, margin, error correction, logo in the middle (forces level H), PNG and SVG, warnings for low contrast, light-on-dark, small margin and dense codes. The QR encoder is written in Vault (graphics/qrEncode.mjs), no new package. Both new routes are behind the paid-tool guard and daily limit and have cost previews (tool=expand, tool=subject). Ask Graphics can plan AI fill. Tooltips, help boxes, subtitles, the How Graphics works box, the Graphics guide catalogue, the User Guide, Ctrl+K aliases and docs updated; tool count 43 to 44.
entries.benefit: Pictures can be reframed to social shapes without borders or cropping away content; subject cut-outs and background removal inside the editing tools take one click; QR codes for posters and packaging no longer need an outside site. No package.json change, so the deploy stays fast. Checked locally: the QR encoder matched the Python segno library module for module on 67 codes (versions 1-40, all levels) and six sample codes decoded with OpenCV, including a contact card, Unicode text and a logo-covered code; Subject / Background selected correctly on screen in all three tools with the local cut-out model; Pad to 16:9 gave the right size; new tests (graphicsExpand, qrEncode) and the existing graphics, tutor, tool-count, cost and nav tests pass; client builds.
entries.concerns: AI fill has NOT been run against the real FAL model: the stitching was tested with a stub, so how convincing the painted space looks (people or text cut by the edge, large additions) is unknown, and each try costs about $0.025. Select subject on the live site goes through Replicate (about $0.02 a picture, same call as Background) and was only run locally with the free model. Eraser was browser-only; its two new buttons send the picture to the server (the screen says so). No QR code has been test-scanned with a phone yet. A see-through picture loses its transparency with AI fill (flattened to white). Recolor did not get the subject buttons. The local dev server on port 3001 did not reload the new routes by itself; a restart is needed to try them locally.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Video Tools: HDR colour fix, smart cut, two-pass loudness, Clean up tools
entries.goal: Fix washed-out colour on phone HDR video in every tool, make three existing tools more accurate, and add four clean-up tools, using recipes from the ffmpeg-skill project (MIT) rewritten on Vault's own ffmpeg helpers.
entries.whatChanged: HDR uploads (iPhone default) are tone-mapped to normal colour once before any tool runs (writeUpload, Join, Clip from a link, Replace a section), capped at 1080p; File info shows HDR. Clip "keep original quality" is a smart cut (only the ends re-encoded, middle copied by exact packet count, checked by length and full decode, else the old stream copy). Normalize audio is two-pass with 48 kHz output. New Clean up group: Remove pauses, Stabilise, Reduce grain, Remove logo (draw a box). /api/videos/status lists which optional ffmpeg filters exist. Job cards: captions job starts with Remove pauses, brand job with Remove logo, new "Fix shaky or grainy phone footage" card. Tutor catalogue, voice commands and docs updated.
entries.benefit: Measured locally on ffmpeg-made test clips: HDR picture match 15.9 to 23.1 dB through the Convert route; smart cut exact to the frame and 2-4x faster than a full re-encode; Normalize lands on -16.0 LUFS; Remove pauses keeps picture and sound the same length; Stabilise cuts frame-to-frame shake 61%; Remove logo fills the box cleanly. All four new tools run end to end in the browser against a local server. No new packages or Dockerfile change, so a fast deploy.
entries.concerns: Not tried on a real iPhone file; all test clips were synthetic. Smart-cut files not played in Safari or on an iPhone, and most iPhone video (HEVC) falls back to the old copy. HDR above 1080p now comes out at 1080p. The HDR conversion adds an extra encode for HDR uploads, which could push long 4K clips toward the five-minute request limit. Stabilise takes about twice as long as other tools and is not a background job. Reduce grain strengths were tuned on synthetic grain and can soften fine detail. The Railway ffmpeg filters (zscale, vidstab) are expected from Debian but unconfirmed until /api/videos/status is checked after deploy. Separately noticed: all /api/videos routes share a 30-per-minute limit, which quick tool switching can use up.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF to Word: move running headers/footers out of the body on every page
entries.goal: Stop converted Word files getting an extra empty page that holds only the previous page footer.
entries.whatChanged: Running header/footer text (top or bottom 8% of a page, repeated on other pages) is now removed from every page before pdf2docx parses, not only from pages where a guessed table had broken the layout, and put back as Word header/footer frames at the PDF position. Fonts and cell fills are read from the original PDF. Pages where a guessed table still slices text are re-parsed with table guessing off.
entries.benefit: LibreOffice press kit converts to 7 pages (PDF 7, was 8 with an empty page 2). On the 14 test PDFs no file lost words and no page count went up. Checked by rendering in Word locally.
entries.concerns: More documents now get their header/footer as Word frames. On a drawing set the repeated title block (Project, Drawing No.) is treated as footer: it looks the same but its text sits in the footer over the table lines instead of in the table cells. Frames are absolutely positioned, so changing the page size in Word will not move them. Not yet tested on the Railway server.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF to Word: keep lost spaces and outlined headings
entries.goal: Stop words running together in converted Word files, and stop headings disappearing from LibreOffice-made PDFs.
entries.whatChanged: pdf2docx text extraction is wrapped. Spans that are only spaces are attached to their neighbour, because pdf2docx dropped them and Chrome/LibreOffice often put the space between words in its own span (text alternates between two subsets of one font). Invisible text covered by letter-sized filled shapes (LibreOffice exports some headings as outlines plus invisible text) is kept and given the shapes colour; invisible OCR text over a scanned image is still dropped.
entries.benefit: On the 14 test PDFs, share of PDF words that come through intact in Word: Kogan bill 62% to 99.4%, LibreOffice press kit 93.6% to 100% (headings like Fact sheet & specifications and Press release are back, in red), Chrome press kit 98.5% to 100%. No file got worse; page counts unchanged. Checked by rendering in Word locally.
entries.concerns: Rescued outlined headings come out in the right colour but not bold. The LibreOffice press kit still gets an empty page 2 (pre-existing pdf2docx issue). Wraps a private pdf2docx method; if a future pdf2docx renames it the repair is skipped with a note, not a failure. Not yet tested on the Railway server.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF to Word: keep header/footer text, stop false cell fills
entries.goal: Make the two earlier PDF to Word repairs safe on PDFs other than the press kit, after a 14-PDF test showed they dropped header/footer text and painted cells wrongly.
entries.whatChanged: Header/footer lines removed by the footer repair are now put back as each page Word header/footer, as floating frames at their PDF position so they take no body space; duplicate overprinted lines are skipped. The cell-fill repair now only applies when the dark shape covers the whole text, is about the width of the cell and the height of its row, contains no image or other shape (thin dividers allowed), and the cell holds no nested table.
entries.benefit: On 14 test PDFs (press kits, invoices, brochures, guides, bills) the new version keeps as many of the PDF words as plain pdf2docx on every file. Page counts: press kit 6 (PDF 6, was 7), questionnaire 14 (PDF 13, was 22), TPG invoice 4 (PDF 4, was 5); the others are unchanged. Checked by rendering every result in Word locally.
entries.concerns: Pre-existing pdf2docx limits remain: words run together on some Chrome and LibreOffice PDFs, an empty page on one LibreOffice file, odd background blocks, invisible numbers in small circles. Repaired pages are parsed twice, so a 4-page invoice took 32s instead of 22s (limit 180s). Header/footer frames are positioned absolutely, so editing the page size in Word will not move them. Not yet tested on the Railway server.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF to Word: restore dropped header cell fill
entries.goal: Make the press kit Fact Sheet DETAILS header readable: pdf2docx dropped its red background, leaving white text on white.
entries.whatChanged: After conversion, a table cell holding only light text with no shading gets the fill of the dark shape found behind that text in the PDF. A cell with no text of its own that only wraps a shaded nested table (how pdf2docx builds the first header cell) takes the same fill, so the header bar has no white gap. Colours are matched within rounding, since pdf2docx and PyMuPDF round the same red differently. The script now reports cellsShaded.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: PDF to Word: repair sliced text and nameless fonts

entries.whatChanged: After pdf2docx parses the PDF, any page where a guessed (stream) table cuts through a line of text, or reaches into the running header/footer, is parsed again with that page header/footer text removed; if it is still cut, that page is parsed with table guessing off. Nameless Type3 fonts (Chrome/Skia PDFs) are classified from their rendered l/I glyphs: serif feet become Georgia, otherwise Arial; thick stem sets bold, slant sets italic. The script reports which pages were repaired and which fonts were replaced. Also used by Document Redaction PDF intake.

entries.subject: PDF Tools: PDF to Word with pdf2docx instead of LibreOffice
entries.goal: PDF → Word turned a 7-page PDF into a one-page Word file: LibreOffice's PDF import puts every line in a positioned text box and its .docx export stacks all pages onto page 1.
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/pdfToWord (pdf_to_docx.py run with python3, wrapped by pdfToDocx() in index.js). POST /api/pdf/pdf-to-office (server/routes/pdf.js) now converts docx through pdf2docx, and odt as pdf2docx then LibreOffice docx → odt; .txt still uses LibreOffice. If pdf2docx is not installed yet it falls back to LibreOffice and logs a warning. entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: AI Visibility: AU search, honest fetch identity, fewer false positives
entries.goal: Fix five problems seen in a real wiwc.com.au report: US search results for an Australian business, a browser check that failed with ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR, the descriptive brand "Walk-In Wine Cabinets Australia" matching any answer about walk-in wine cabinets, a LocalBusiness with areaServed flagged as a Fix for missing address, and many repeated "Not checked" schema rows. Testing also showed robots.txt reported as missing when it exists.
entries.whatChanged: searchClient.js: Brave adds country=AU&search_lang=en, Serper sends gl au / hl en. render.js: the hardcoded Chrome 124 user agent is gone; userAgentFor() uses the real Chromium version, because wiwc's firewall drops a browser whose user agent does not match it. aiVisibilityService.js: when the page or robots.txt fetch is refused, it retries with an honest "VaultAI/1.0 (AI visibility audit)" identity; robots.txt failures say "could not be read" instead of "not found" (markdown.js and the page). queryAnalysis.js: legal suffixes no longer strip words like Australia or Group, the two-word short form is dropped, and any brand variant that appears in the question itself (plural-insensitive) is ignored. schema.js: a LocalBusiness with areaServed needs no street address and is shown as complete (service area); with neither, a warning offers both options and costs 10 points; unchecked entities fold into one row per type with a count (Country x7). Tests and docs/ai-visibility.md updated.
entries.benefit: Australian businesses are ranked against Australian results, sites behind strict firewalls (like wiwc) can now be rendered and their robots.txt read, descriptive brand names no longer give false "named" results, service-area businesses are not told to publish a street address, and the schema table is short enough to read. On wiwc locally: render works (about 650 words), robots.txt read (only /wp-admin/ blocked), structured data 88 instead of 63.
entries.concerns: The Australian search settings were not checked against a live search: the local Brave and Serper keys are invalid. Assistant answers are still unverified for the same reason. The honest VaultAI fallback means some sites will see a non-browser visitor and may block it. Dropping brand variants that appear in the question can miss a real mention when the brand name is the question's own words; the full brand and domain label still count. When search and assistants cannot run, the overall score covers only technical areas and can look high (95 on wiwc locally). wiwc's firewall may also block real AI crawlers whose user agents contain "Mozilla"; not tested.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: AI Visibility: ask real AI assistants, honest search errors, background runs
entries.goal: Make AI Visibility measure what it says it measures. A review found the citation check was really a top-five search ranking check (a model answered only from the top five Brave results), that search errors such as an invalid key were reported as "site not found", that failed steps were averaged in as zero, and that a run could outlast the gateway timeout.
entries.whatChanged: Each buyer question now gets two separate checks. Search ranking: one live search, top 10, scored by position (#1 100, top 3 85, top 5 70, top 10 50). Real AI assistants (new server/services/aiVisibility/assistants.js): Claude with the Anthropic web search tool, Gemini grounded with Google Search, and Perplexity (Sonar API) when PERPLEXITY_API_KEY is set; each searches for itself and the report says per assistant whether it named the business and whether a site page was among its sources. Models come from the workspace model list (Perplexity from setting ai_visibility_perplexity_model, default sonar). New GET /api/ai-visibility/assistants drives tick boxes on the new-audit screen. Scores are now six areas: technical 20, readability 15, structured data 15, search ranking 15, named by AI assistants 25, key facts 10. Fixes: searchClient providerError() recognises Brave/Serper/SerpAPI error shapes and HTTP errors (also used by the chat @search route in server/routes/webSearch.js); unmeasured values are no longer averaged as zero; brand matching covers short forms, legal suffixes and the domain label and never uses a page name like Home; subdomains count as the site; template questions no longer cut a hyphenated brand and are flagged in the report; key facts are checked against assistant answers only; the fetch retry no longer pretends to be Googlebot; provider errors are shortened to a readable line. Audits run in the background: POST /audits answers 202 with a running row, columns status/progress/error added in server/db.js (rows still running at boot are marked failed), the page polls every 3 seconds, shows each step, offers Run again on failure, and allows one running audit per person (409). Version 1 reports still render as before, labelled as the earlier version. Markdown/PDF, guide chat catalogue, tools list, docs/ai-visibility.md and docs/env-vars.md updated; tests extended.
entries.benefit: The report now separates search ranking from what real AI assistants actually say, a bad or exhausted search key is named as the cause instead of showing a false "not found" failure, the score only counts what was measured, and long runs no longer depend on one request staying open.
entries.concerns: No real assistant answer has been seen yet: the local Anthropic, Gemini and Brave keys were invalid, so the Claude web search call, Gemini Google Search grounding and Perplexity call are written from documentation and checked only through their failure paths and unit tests on response shapes. Perplexity has never been called at all. Verified locally in a real browser: the form with tick boxes, the running screen (leaving and returning), failure screen with Run again, the 409 for a second run, private-address blocking, an old version 1 report, and the success layout using a made-up local test row (deleted afterwards). Cost per audit goes up: one search plus one paid call per ticked assistant per question, and Anthropic bills each web search on top of tokens. A run lives in the server process, so a deploy or restart mid-run marks it failed. Answers vary between runs, so results are a sample. The chat @search route now returns 502 with the provider message where it used to return 500 or an empty list.

entries.goal: Give AI Visibility the same round guide chat every other app page has, and stop a site that drops the first connection from surfacing a raw socket hang up error.

It says it only audits and reports, checks one public page at a time, that key-fact matching is a heuristic, and that an audit is a snapshot it cannot control what an AI assistant says; it sees no address, score or report. client/src/pages/aiVisibility/aiVisibilityTools.mjs is the list the page and guide share; client/src/pages/aiVisibility/AiVisibilityTutorChat.jsx is the wrapper; AiVisibilityPage.jsx marks each part with data-guide, passes currentTool, and openToolById scrolls there (a report part needs a saved audit open, otherwise a toast says to open one). entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: AI Visibility: audit how AI assistants find, read and cite a page
entries.goal: Add a Web & SEO tool that answers a different question from SEO or Page speed: when someone asks an AI assistant about this business, can the assistant reach the page, read the offer without JavaScript, understand the entity, and cite it?
entries.whatChanged: New page /ai-visibility (nav Web & SEO → AI Visibility, icon radar, flag aiVisibility default off with lifecycle preview, so admins can trial it). One run: fetches the page with the shared SSRF-safe htmlFetch; fetches and parses robots.txt; checks each AI crawler separately (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, Bingbot, Bytespider, meta-externalagent) and names the exact Allow/Disallow rule that decides each one; renders the same page in Chromium and compares raw-HTML words with rendered words to show how much of the offer exists only after JavaScript (unmeasured, not zero, if Chromium fails); extracts and validates JSON-LD entity by entity (Organization, LocalBusiness and subtypes, Product, Offer, FAQPage, Article, BreadcrumbList, WebSite, Service) with required and useful properties; then runs up to six buyer questions — supplied, or four generated from the page title/description/headings with a template fallback — through the existing SEARCH_API_KEY search (Brave/Serper/SerpAPI) and a connected text model answer grounded in those results. Each question reports three separate verdicts: found in the search results and at what position, named in the answer (brand or domain), linked in the answer (a URL on the host). Optional key facts are matched against answers and snippets with a documented heuristic (numbers must appear with a compatible unit, a range needs both ends, at least 60% of distinctive words). Weighted scores: technical 25, no-JS readability 15, structured data 20, citation 25, accuracy 15; an area that could not be measured is left out and the remaining weights rescaled. Suggestions ordered fail/improve/consider with a concrete action. Saved runs in new table ai_visibility_audits, on-page report, Copy for AI (Markdown) and a server-rendered PDF (pdf-lib, standard fonts). Router mounted at /api/ai-visibility with requireFeature('aiVisibility'); aiLimiter on the POST only so list/get/markdown/pdf do not consume the AI budget. Client page with search/sort/delete sidebar, new-audit form (URL, name, brand, model, questions, facts), feature-gate redirect and help modal. Tests: npm run test:ai-visibility, covering robots grouping/matching, JSON-LD, fact matching, scoring (including unmeasured areas) and Markdown. Docs: docs/ai-visibility.md, docs/features.md, docs/key-files.md and the user guide.
entries.benefit: One deliberate audit shows the failures that ordinary SEO tools miss: a crawler blocked in robots.txt, an offer that only exists after JavaScript, a half-filled JSON-LD block that teaches an answer engine the wrong thing, a site that ranks but is never named, or an answer that states 0.5 amps where the page says 0.5°C. The three citation verdicts keep those different failures apart, and unmeasured areas are left out of the score instead of dragging it down.
entries.concerns: Not run against a real model or search key on Railway: the pure modules are tested, the client builds, but no live audit has been seen end to end, so provider responses, timings and Railway's Chromium launch are unverified. A run costs one search call per question plus one model call each and can take a minute or two; the POST is rate-limited but a member can still start several runs. Fact matching is a heuristic, not entailment, and the report says so. The renderer re-checks every request with checkSsrf, but Chromium resolves names itself after the check, so a hostile DNS server that answers differently a second time is not fully covered — the same accepted trade-off as brandFromUrl. The flag defaults off (admins can always open it), so a trial is required before members see it.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Page speed: Copy for AI replaces the single-device report copy
entries.goal: Make the least useful report output earn its place: the single-device Copy this report button only repeated Copy mobile + desktop, so it now gives an AI assistant a ready-to-paste improvement brief.

entries.subject: Device preview: show every picture, including style-file backgrounds
entries.goal: Stop pictures being blocked in Device preview (reported on finestone.com.au, including pictures served from Amazon S3).
entries.whatChanged: The preview can only show data: pictures (Vault's Content-Security-Policy), so every picture has to be fetched by the server and inlined. Three gaps fixed. server/services/webExtractorService.js: fetchBinary treats a hang-up (socket hang up, ECONNRESET, EPROTO) as a refusal and tries the next identity, with a curl identity added last; finestone's firewall hangs up on browser-like identities, so all 12 of its own pictures failed. server/services/restyle/inlineImages.js: limits raised to 5 MB a picture (was 2.5; the S3 banner is 3.9 MB), 20 MB in all (was 12) and 60 pictures (was 40); inlineImagesInCss takes imagesOnly (skips font files) and a shared budget (newBudget). server/routes/restyle.js: /fetch-url accepts inlineCssImages, which inlines pictures in the linked style files (inlineLinkedCssImages) and notes any that failed; client/src/pages/DevicePreviewPage.jsx sends it. Test added to restyleLoad.test.js; docs/restyle.md and docs/key-files.md updated, including why the console's 'Blocked script execution in about:srcdoc' line is harmless.
entries.benefit: On finestone.com.au all 44 page pictures and 20 of 22 style-file backgrounds now inline (the other 2 are files the page never shows), and a screenshot under Vault's picture rules showed all 41 images with no blocked-picture messages. Web Extractor and the Style editor get the retry-on-hang-up and the higher limits too.
entries.concerns: Bigger responses: finestone's /fetch-url answer is about 23 MB, because inlined pictures are base64, so a page loads slower on a slow connection and uses more server memory while it is built. Checked from a home connection, not from Railway, where the site's firewall may behave differently. Not seen in the running Vault app (no local login session); checked by running the same loader and preview code in a headless browser with the same picture policy. Font files are still not inlined, so icon fonts from sites that do not send CORS headers can still show as boxes.

entries.subject: Device preview: load every style file, show hidden content, retry dropped renders

Loading up to 40 files makes big pages slower to load and the response larger (8 MB CSS cap). The 'Worth knowing' box and the full Device preview page were not seen in the running app (no local login session); the preview document itself was screenshotted. entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Page speed: estimated score gain for each action
entries.goal: Show the owner, before anything is fixed, roughly how many points each Page speed action would add to the score, so effort can go where the gain is.
entries.whatChanged: server/services/htmlLighthouse.js: each finding now stores its category weight (from the category's auditRefs) and Lighthouse's metricSavings (LCP/FCP/TBT/CLS), and each view stores categoryWeights (total weight per category). New client/src/pages/pageSpeed/scoreImpact.mjs (+ test): Lighthouse 10-12 log-normal scoring curves and weights for mobile and desktop; perfGain() takes a finding's savings off the lab timings and re-scores; checkGain() gives weight x (1 - score) / total x 100 for Accessibility, Best practices and SEO; combinedImpact() totals a set of actions (performance savings per timing: largest plus half of the rest, as fixes overlap; capped at 100). pageSpeedActions.mjs: buildActions() adds impact to each action and sorts each priority group by biggest gain; impactText()/combinedText() for Copy and PDF. HtmlAuditPage.jsx: green badge per action (~ marks a performance estimate) with a tooltip explaining exact vs estimate, a box at the top of the Actions tab with 'Fix first list only' and 'Everything still to do' as score from -> to (ticked actions left out), totals beside each group heading, and a 'run this page again' line for older runs. PDF report: the badge on each card and a 'scores could become' line per device. Guide chat catalogue gains 'Score estimates'; (i) box text and docs/html-agent.md updated.
entries.benefit: The owner can see which fixes move the score most and what the scores could become once the list is done, on screen and in the client PDF.
entries.concerns: Only runs made after this deploy have estimates (older saved runs lack weights and savings; the page says to run again). Performance figures are estimates: they depend on Google's own predicted savings, overlap between fixes is handled by a rule of thumb, and lab scores vary a few points run to run. The scoring curves are Lighthouse 10-12's; if Google changes them the performance estimate drifts until updated. The formula was checked against Lighthouse's reference points and the screens/PDF seen on local dev with synthetic data, not yet against a live PageSpeed run, so the weights and metricSavings fields from the real API are assumed, not seen.
