entries.subject: Page speed: plain-English "Where on the page" for each action
entries.goal: Make the evidence under each Page speed action readable for a person: the owner said the raw developer detail (CSS selectors with the same long explanation repeated on every line) needed formatting for humans.
entries.whatChanged: client/src/pages/pageSpeed/pageSpeedActions.mjs: humanEvidence() turns each Lighthouse item into { where, detail, code }: element kind from the tag (Link, Picture, Button...), its name from visible label or class/id, the page area from words in the selector (header, menu, footer, gallery, products, banner, back-to-top...), where a link goes (from href), file name and host for file items, sizes in KB/MB and ms instead of raw bytes, contrast colours. explanationGroups() splits the axe 'Fix all / Fix any of the following' text into two short lists, shown once per action instead of on every line. cleanLighthouseText() drops the dangling 'Learn more/how...' sentence and [attr] code marks. buildActions() reads the structured items from the source audit (old runs fall back to parsing the stored evidence strings), dedupes them and adds where, flagged, docsUrl and cleaned technical text. HtmlAuditPage.jsx: a 'Where on the page' list on each action card (first five, Show all), the For your developer block rebuilt (Google's text once, guide link, Why Google flagged these, Code to look for with the selector and HTML in small code boxes), Report tab findings use the same plain lines with the code in a hover tip. Copy action list and the PDF report (pageSpeedReportPdf.jsx) include the locations; the PDF's developer detail lists the code once as a numbered list.
entries.benefit: An owner or client can see which links, pictures or files are affected and where on the page, without reading CSS selectors; the developer still gets the exact code, without the repeated boilerplate. Works on existing saved runs.
entries.concerns: Names come from the site's own class names, so a vaguely named element reads as e.g. Link inside "footarea" (the area and link target help). The area guess is keyword-based and can be wrong on unusual class names. Seen on screen and in the PDF on local dev with the owner's real evidence pasted into a test run, not against a fresh live PageSpeed result.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: CRM email log: ignore drafts, read whole threads, show first and last dates
entries.goal: Fix client email entries that showed the wrong date, subject and counts (found on a real thread), and show the dates of the first and last email.
entries.whatChanged: In server/services/clientEmailSync.js: (1) an unsent draft, or mail in the bin or spam, no longer counts as an email, nor moves the entry's date or subject, nor appears in the summary (an unsent reply in Drafts had been counted as received, dating the entry today with an empty "Re:" subject); a thread that is only a draft is not logged. (2) Each thread the Gmail search finds is now read whole (threads.get, one call per thread instead of one per message), so the counts and the first and last dates cover the full exchange even when only one new message fell inside the search window (a re-read had rebuilt a 7-email thread from one message). (3) The subject is the first email's, even when blank, so a thread started from a phone with no subject stays "(no subject)" (the previous change had wrongly skipped to the first message with a subject). (4) The note reads, for example, 5 sent, 2 received (7 emails), first 6 Nov 2026, last 9 Nov 2026, then the summary, with three-letter months in Brisbane time. (5) An entry this job wrote and nobody edited (its note starts with its own subject) is brought in line with the whole thread on the next read: counts, dates and subject are corrected and its existing summary is kept with no new model call, unless the thread has new mail. An entry whose note the person wrote is left alone until its thread grows. docs/crm-email-sync.md and the CRM guide describe it.
entries.benefit: Entries show the true number of emails and the real first and last dates, and a draft you have open can no longer change them. Entries already logged wrongly repair themselves.
entries.concerns: Tested with a fake Gmail (a draft in a thread, a thread read whole when only the newest message is in the window, a damaged entry repaired with its summary kept, an edited note left alone); not run against a real mailbox, so the real test is pressing Check email now on the client that showed the wrong entry. Reading a thread whole means a thread with many messages is read in full even if one is new (one call per thread). The daily job and Check email now will rewrite the date and note of every entry this job wrote that disagrees with its thread, once. A person who edited an entry by changing only part of its note (keeping the first line) will have it treated as unedited and overwritten on the next read.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: CRM email log: real subject, day span and an AI summary per thread
entries.goal: Make the logged email entries readable: fix the "(no subject)" threads, show how long a thread ran, and summarise what the exchange was about.
entries.whatChanged: In server/services/clientEmailSync.js the subject is now the first message in a thread that has one (a blank first message made a whole thread "(no subject)"). The note shows the days a thread ran over in Brisbane time (for example 6-9 Nov; nothing when it was all one day) after the sent/received counts, and a 2 to 4 sentence summary of the exchange written by the light model (getModelsForUser().light, usage logged as clients_email_summary). The model is shown the thread text (quoted earlier mail and reply trails removed, about 9,000 characters across the thread) only to write the summary; the message text is not stored, only the summary. The prompt treats email text as data, not instructions, and asks it not to repeat passwords or card or account numbers. A thread is summarised when first logged and when it grows, at most 40 per client per run; an entry this job wrote that has no summary yet (logged before this change, or a failed attempt) gets one on the next read of its client as long as its note was not edited. If the model fails the entry is logged without a summary and retried. docs/crm-email-sync.md and the CRM guide text describe it.
entries.benefit: Each email entry says what the exchange was about and what is outstanding, instead of a bare subject and counts.
entries.concerns: PRIVACY AND COST: to write a summary the text of your client emails is sent to the AI model provider (it is not stored here, only the summary is). One model call per thread, up to 40 per client per run, and the first run over many threads costs the most; usage shows under clients_email_summary. Existing entries get a summary the next time their client is read (the daily run or Check email now), so a large first pass may take a while. Tested with a fake Gmail and a fake model (subject choice, day span, quote stripping, prompt shape, failure gives no summary, retry, edited notes left alone); never run with a real model or real mail, so how good the summaries read is unchecked. Summary quality depends on the light model and on how much of a long thread fits in the 9,000 characters. A summary is not rewritten when nothing new arrives, so one that reads poorly stays until the thread grows.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: CRM: log client email from Gmail into Activity, back to 1 July 2026
entries.goal: Stop the Activity log depending on remembering to type emails in: record the email exchanged with a client's people automatically, including everything since 1 July 2026.
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/clientEmailSync.js and server/cron/clientEmailSyncCron.js. A client is matched by its contacts' email addresses (exact) and by email domains saved on the client (new Email domains field on New client and Edit client; free-mail domains such as gmail.com are refused, a pasted website address is tidied to its domain). Inbox and sent mail is read from the person's own connected Gmail (existing read-only permission) and kept as one Activity entry per Gmail thread (type email, source gmail_sync): subject and a sent/received count only, never the message text; newsletters and automated mail are skipped. Each entry carries externalId thread:<id> with a unique index, so nothing is logged twice, a grown thread moves its entry on, and an entry the person edited is left alone until its thread grows. Every client starts unread, so the first daily run seeds all existing clients back to 1 July 2026 (Brisbane); creating a client with a domain, adding or changing a contact email, or changing the domain list marks that client unread and reads it back to 1 July straight away in the background. The daily job runs at 21:00 UTC (7:00 am Brisbane), before the stale-deal check, under withCronLock, and only where external cron is on. New: POST /api/clients/:id/email-sync and a Check email now button with a status line at the top of the Info card. New columns clients.emailDomains, clients.emailSyncedAt, client_interactions.externalId. A Gmail login failure in the daily run raises a Suggestions alert. docs/crm-email-sync.md, the CRM guide and related docs describe it.
entries.benefit: The activity log fills itself with the real email history for each client, and a new client or contact is filled back to 1 July without any extra step. It also stops the stale-deal flag raising a deal you are actively emailing about.
entries.concerns: NEVER RUN AGAINST A REAL GMAIL ACCOUNT: it was tested with a fake Gmail (rules, and a real database sync: first read goes back to 1 July, later reads are incremental, no duplicates, a grown thread updates, another person's client is not read) and on screen for the domain field (a free-mail domain is refused, a pasted URL is tidied) and the Check email now button with Gmail not connected. Gmail's own search behaviour (the from:@domain match, sent mail, the after: time) and header names are as documented but unproven here, so the first live read, for example Check email now on a client with a domain, is the real test. The first daily run reads every client of every person with Gmail connected, back to 1 July: up to 500 messages per client, one Gmail call per message, so it can take a while and use quota. A deleted email entry comes back the next time its thread is read (there is no memory of deletions). Domain matching includes everyone at the domain, so a client's staff you never email still count if they email you. Anyone whose Gmail is connected gets this, and mail from known contacts and domains is copied (subject only) into the database. Three small columns are added at boot and the cron is off on staging. The ownership tests and the cross-user route manifest pass (one new route, authed).

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: CRM: flag stale deals in the Suggestions inbox
entries.goal: Notice an open deal that has gone quiet, instead of it sitting unseen in the Pipeline.
entries.whatChanged: New server/services/staleDeals.js and server/cron/staleDealsCron.js, started from server/index.js. Daily at 22:00 UTC (8:00 am Brisbane), under withCronLock, every open deal (not won or lost, client not archived) with no sign of life for 21 days gets one Suggestions card (alert, source staleDeals, linked to the client). Sign of life is the later of the deal's last edit and the client's latest logged call, email or note; deal-stage and contact-added rows do not count. The card is keyed on the deal id, so a repeat run updates it and an Ignored card stays quiet. It sends nothing and calls no paid service, so it runs on every server, including where external cron is switched off. Test: node server/services/staleDeals.test.js.
entries.benefit: A quiet deal is raised to you rather than relying on remembering to look.
entries.concerns: The 21-day limit is a constant (STALE_DAYS), not a setting. A card is not removed when the deal is touched or closed; it is dismissed by hand. Checked with a unit test and by running the real query and capture against the local database (one card for the stale deal, none for the fresh one, a second run updated rather than duplicated); the scheduled job itself did not fire locally. Staging and production share the code, so if they share a database both will raise the same cards (the key stops duplicates). Documentation for this commit is in the next commit.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Plans: a client project's dates follow its plans
entries.goal: Stop a client project's start and target end dates drifting away from the plans that schedule its work, without ever overwriting dates the person typed.
entries.whatChanged: A client project's start and target end dates now follow the plans filed under it: the earliest start and the latest finish of its draft and active plans that have dates (server/services/projectPlanDates.js; a plan that is Done, Archived or undated does not count). They stay the project's own columns, so the Client work list, Notes' related items and the Tasks timeline show them with no change. The first time plans take over, the typed dates are kept in new columns ownStartDate and ownTargetEndDate (with datesFollowPlans, default true, and datesDerived) and are put back when the plans go away (deleted, archived, done, or nothing dated), when following is switched off, and the plan's dates return on Undo of a plan delete. A different date typed by hand in PUT /api/projects/:id switches following off; the same dates sent back change nothing. The sync runs on plan create, update (old and new project), step add, change and delete, dependency add and remove, plan delete and restore, and can never fail a plan change. New route PUT /api/client-projects/:id/dates-mode { follow }. The client project Brief shows "from its plans" with Use my own dates, or Follow its plans when off, and disables its date boxes while they come from plans. The Plans and CRM guides, the (i) text and docs/plans.md were updated.
entries.benefit: Project dates in Client work and the Tasks timeline stay true to the actual plans, and the person can always get their own dates back.
entries.concerns: Writes to the project's own date columns, so every screen that shows them changes for any client project that has a dated plan; the generic project save (routes/projects.js) gained a hook that runs whenever a date is sent, so a mistake there could affect saving any project. The first takeover keeps the typed dates, but a project whose dates were typed AFTER plans took over (following off) has no stored copy of the plan dates. Four columns are added to projects at boot. Checked on screen only with test data (one client, one project, one plan, the two buttons), and by a real-database test; on a machine in a non-UTC timezone the Brief shows a plain date one day early (existing behaviour of its date formatting, the database value is right). The generic project form (ProjectDetail) does not say the dates come from plans; saving a different date there just turns following off. Not run on Railway.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Plans: file plans under clients and client projects
entries.goal: Let a plan belong to a CRM client and to one of that client's projects, so client work shows its plans and the tasks that come from them.
entries.whatChanged: plans gets "clientId" (FK clients) and "clientProjectId" (FK projects, a projects row with projectType client), both ON DELETE SET NULL, added in db.js right after the clients table is created. resolveClientLink in plans.js checks both are the caller's own, that a project belongs to the chosen client, that naming only a project chooses its client, that changing the client without naming a project drops a project of the old client, and that clearing the client clears the project; an ordinary chat workspace is refused as a client project. A plan made from a note starts with the note's client (and its project when that is a client project), shown in the box and overridable; tasks sent from a plan are created with the plan's client and project (tasks.clientId and projectId). GET /api/plans takes clientId and clientProjectId filters, and plan and list rows carry clientName and clientProjectName; create, update and the from-diagram and from-note routes accept the two fields (no new routes). Screens: Client and Client project boxes (PlanClientPicker.jsx) on the plan, in the Start a plan box and in the Make a plan box; a client filter and a chip on each Plans list card, with /plans?client= and ?clientProject= opening it filtered; a Plans section with New plan and Open in Plans on a client's page and a client project's page (ClientPlans.jsx). The Plans guide (21 controls), the CRM guide (a plans control), the Plans (i) box and docs/plans.md were updated.
entries.benefit: Plans, and the tasks sent from them, show up under the right client and client project, and a note filed under a client makes plans for that client without re-entering it.
entries.concerns: Adds two columns and two indexes to plans at boot (additive, idempotent). Tasks already sent are not moved if a plan's client changes later. Checked on screen only with test data (one client, one client project, one note), not a real client with many projects; the Client pickers load every client and client project once per box, which is fine for dozens but untested for hundreds. The client and project sections are left out when the CRM or Plans is off for the person, which was seen only for the on case. The CRM guide page test passes but the new Plans section was not added to the CRM tour. No new routes, so routeManifest.json is unchanged.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Plans: make a plan from a note
entries.goal: Let a note that already holds a checklist or outline become a dated plan without retyping it, the way a diagram already can.
entries.whatChanged: A Make a plan button in an open note (editor toolbar beside Convert to Task, shown only when Plans is on) turns the note's headings and lists into a plan with no AI. Rules in server/services/planFromNote.js: a heading becomes a section (group) and a list item a step, indented items become sub-steps, a length at the end of a line ("(3 days)", 3d, 2 weeks at five working days) is used and removed from the name, a ticked check-box is a step already Done, a line starting Milestone: is a milestone, paragraphs, quotes, code and empty bullets are ignored, a heading with nothing under it is dropped. An Order choice decides what waits on what: as the lists say (numbered lists run in order, bullets together; the default), one after another, or all together; links are kept to the minimum. Up to 60 steps and the first 30,000 characters. The same box as diagrams (start, finish-by, working week, days per step, live fit line, Estimate lengths with AI, which skips steps whose length the note gave) opens; Create plan makes the plan with its nested groups, steps, dependencies and a plan_links row (kind note) in one transaction, after checking the note is the caller's, and the button then reads In a plan. New routes POST /api/plans/from-note/preview, /from-note/estimate and /from-note (named, before /:id); GET /api/plans/by-source already handled kind note. The diagram and note paths now share previewFromDraft / createFromPreview in plans.js and a draft's steps can carry parentRef, hintDays and status. PlanButton and MakePlanDialog were generalised (their title props renamed to sourceTitle). Notes: a tip (NOTE_TIPS.makePlan), a guide entry (make-plan, notesTools.mjs and notesTutor.js together) and a Plans section in the (i) box; the Plans guide (20 controls), its (i) box and docs updated.
entries.benefit: A checklist or outline in a note becomes a plan in one step, with the lengths already written in it, and the note and plan link to each other.
entries.concerns: Only tried on a local copy with one test note (plus real-database and pure tests); real notes with messier writing are untried, and a line whose trailing number is not a length (for example "Call builder 3 days later") would be read as a length. The refactor touched the diagram path (shared preview and create code), which still passes its tests. The Notes compass tour has no step for the new button, and on a phone the button shows its words while the rest of the Notes toolbar is icons only. The AI estimate for notes has only been exercised with a stand-in model. A plan made from a note is a copy: later edits to the note are not copied into it. The 3 new routes were added to routeManifest.json by hand.

The AI estimate has only been exercised with a stand-in model; a real model's numbers and wording are untried, and the local database has no model so the button shows "No AI model is set up" there. entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Plans: send steps to Tasks
entries.goal: Let a plan step become a real task, so planned work shows up in Tasks (and its calendar and timeline views) when the person chooses, without plan steps ever leaking into Tasks by themselves.
entries.whatChanged: A checklist button on every plan step, and Send all to Tasks above the Steps table with an inline Yes / No, call the new POST /api/plans/:id/send-to-tasks (server/services/planTasks.js, one transaction). The task gets the step's title, the step's last day as its due date, days x 8 hours as the estimate (none for a milestone or group), the milestone flag, the step's status, and notes naming the plan. A group becomes a parent task and its sub-steps become subtasks; waits-on links between sent steps become task_dependencies (skipped if they would close a circle with dependencies already in Tasks). Each task is recorded in plan_links (kind task); a step whose task still exists is not sent twice, and if the task was deleted the stale link is replaced and the step can be sent again. GET /api/plans/:id now returns tasks: { stepId: { taskId, status } }. The button becomes a tick that opens Tasks. A plan with no start date sends tasks with no due date and says how many. The Plans guide (now 18 controls), the (i) box, tooltips and docs/plans.md were updated, and the route added to routeManifest.json.
entries.benefit: Planned work can be put into Tasks in one click, with dates, estimates, subtasks and dependencies, and stays out of Tasks, the digest and the calendar until the person decides.
entries.concerns: A one-way copy: later changes to a plan step are not pushed to the task, and tasks marked done in Tasks do not mark the step done; this is stated in the tooltips, (i) box, guide and docs. Sending creates real rows in tasks (which the digest, attention list and dashboard read), so a plan with many steps adds many tasks at once; the inline Yes / No is the only guard and there is no bulk undo (delete the tasks in Tasks). The route is not recycle-binned. The tick opens Tasks as a whole because Tasks has no per-task link. Checked on screen locally (send one, send all, the result in Tasks tree and timeline) and by a real-database test; not run on Railway. The 11 SERP Tracker routes missing from routeManifest.json (committed earlier) still fail crossUser.test.js and were left alone.

entries.subject: Plans: guide chat, shared help text and docs
entries.goal: Give Plans the same help as the other tools: a guide chat that points at the real controls, descriptions and tooltips on every control, and written documentation.
entries.whatChanged: The Plans guide (round button on /plans, POST /api/plans-tutor behind the plans flag and the AI rate limit, usage feature plans_guide, registered in server/config/guides.js). Its catalogue covers 17 views and controls, with 9 rules and 9 things Plans does not do, and it knows Make a plan from a diagram is a Diagrams button. client/src/pages/plans/plansTools.mjs now holds the views, view tooltips, blurbs, the (i) box text and the guide's control list, shared by the page and the guide; plansTutor.test.js fails if the two drift or if the catalogue stops stating a fact it must not get wrong. The page now uses that text for its blurb and (i) box, and the guide opens a plan view when asked. Tooltips added to the last controls without one (Cancel buttons, the error-state back button). docs/plans.md gained a Help section (the (i) box, tooltips, microphone, guide and descriptions); docs/guide-chat.md and docs/key-files.md updated.
entries.benefit: Someone new to Plans can say what they want and be pointed at the right control, every control explains itself, and the help text cannot quietly disagree with the page.
entries.concerns: The guide was checked on screen only to open and show its intro and four starter questions; no question was sent to a real model (no AI key locally), so its answers are covered only by the test with a stand-in model. Each question to it is one AI call and counts against the AI rate limit. Not built: a guided tour (the compass button and a Settings entry). Menu items in the Make a plan button's list have no tooltip of their own, like the To Notes menu beside it. The new route was added to routeManifest.json by hand.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Plans: make a plan from a diagram
entries.goal: Turn a flowchart in Diagrams into a dated plan without retyping it, asking for the start, the finish-by date and the days each step takes.
entries.whatChanged: A Make a plan button in Diagrams (beside To Notes, shown only when Plans is switched on) reads the boxes and arrows off the board with the existing readDiagram and sends the structure to the server, which applies fixed rules and uses no AI. Each box becomes a step of one working day unless a length is typed; a decision or an end oval becomes a milestone; a Start oval is dropped; each arrow means the next step waits on the one before. Decisions are assumed to be Yes: arrows leaving a decision that say no, and steps only reachable through them, are left out unless a tick includes them. Arrows that loop back to an earlier step are left out and counted because a plan cannot go in circles. A box asks for the start, finish-by date, working week and days per step, with a live line saying whether it fits (from a server preview that saves nothing). Create plan makes the plan, steps, dependencies and the first plan_links row in one transaction, after checking the diagram is the caller's, and the button then reads In a plan with a list to go to. New routes: POST /api/plans/from-diagram/preview, POST /api/plans/from-diagram, GET /api/plans/by-source (named routes before /:id). Also: a milestone now lands on the day the step before it ends instead of the day after, so a decision adds no day to a plan (earlier Plans tests and docs updated); the shared Dialog gains a 2xl size; the Diagrams guide knows the new button.
entries.benefit: A flowchart becomes a plan in one step: the structure comes from the drawing, the person supplies only the dates and lengths, and the plan and the diagram link to each other.
entries.concerns: Checked on screen only with a test diagram inserted straight into the local database (no AI key locally to draw one); a real hand-drawn or AI-drawn diagram on Railway is untried. Every step is one working day until a length is typed, so the first fit line is optimistic; an Estimate lengths button was left out on purpose. The Yes rule is a guess about a person's labels: a No branch labelled something unusual (for example "Out of stock") is kept. The milestone change alters how every plan with milestones is dated, including any made earlier today. The 3 new routes were added to routeManifest.json by hand; crossUser.test.js still fails on 11 SERP Tracker routes committed earlier without a manifest entry. plan_links now holds real rows; the link is only written after the diagram is checked to be the caller's. A later change to a diagram is not copied into a plan already made.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Plans: dated steps with waits-on links, fit check and a Gantt
entries.goal: Give dated, dependent work its own place: a plan of steps with lengths and waits-on links, drawn as a Gantt, ready to be made from a diagram later.
entries.whatChanged: New Plans tool at /plans (flag plans, preview, off by default, in the Workspace menu group). A plan has a start, a finish-by date, a working week and steps. A step has a length in working days, an optional pinned start, a status, a milestone flag and an optional parent group. Dates are worked out by the server: a step starts the working day after the steps it waits on end, circles are refused, a plan says whether it fits its finish date (exactly, with room, or over by N working days), and with an end date but no start it suggests the start. Plan steps live in their own tables (plans, plan_steps, plan_step_deps, plan_links), not in tasks, so the digest, attention list, dashboard and calendar never see them. plan_links is a generic link table for later (send to Tasks, notes, diagrams, calendar); nothing writes to it yet. Deleting a plan goes to the recycle bin with Undo. The Tasks timeline component now accepts a stored startDate, showBlocked and defaultZoom, with Tasks behaviour unchanged. The (i) box, tooltips and microphones are in; docs/plans.md written.
entries.benefit: A place to plan work with real dates and dependencies that does not clutter Tasks, built on the existing timeline and kept open for diagram-to-plan, send-to-Tasks and calendar links.
entries.concerns: Not run on Railway. Not built: making a plan from a diagram (the reason for the tool), send to Tasks, dragging bars, a calendar layer, a tour and guide chat, and a recycle bin for a single step (deleting one step is permanent after a Yes/No prompt). Four new tables are created on boot. The 10 new routes were added to routeManifest.json by hand because the --update run re-ordered the whole file; crossUser.test.js still fails on 11 SERP Tracker routes committed earlier without a manifest entry. plan_links does not check that the thing linked to belongs to the person; the first code that writes links must. Checked on screen locally only for the list, creating a plan, steps, waits-on, fit messages, the timeline, and delete with Undo. The menu section called Workspace now clashes with the renamed chat Workspaces.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Rename Projects to Workspaces in the UI; drop the project brief
entries.goal: Stop calling a named group of chats a Project, a word that belongs to planning and the Gantt idea, and remove the brief fields nobody uses.
entries.whatChanged: On-screen text only: Projects becomes Workspaces in the sidebar, home page, New Workspace modal, detail page, mobile menu, chat list toggle, New Chat modal, Chat page hints, Chat History, Notes, Mood, Settings text, Admin tile, task filter and command palette. The Goal, Problem, Audience, Constraints, Success Criteria and Tone fields are gone from the workspace form and the New Workspace modal, and chat.js no longer adds them to the system prompt or the branch-chat opener. Tech stack, Notes and the type settings stay. Routes (/projects/...), store names, the projects table and its columns are unchanged. noteGroups.test.mjs updated for the new No workspace label.
entries.benefit: One clear word for a chat collection, which frees Project for planning work, and a shorter workspace form with a smaller chat prompt.
entries.concerns: A workspace that already has a goal, problem, audience, constraints, success criteria or tone saved stops sending it to the AI; the data is kept but now unreachable from the screen, and production was not checked. Some project wording remains in the Settings tour mock-up, tour text and UserGuidePage body text. Home cards still show an old goal if one was saved. Checked on screen locally on the sidebar, home page, New Workspace modal and detail page only; Chat, Notes, Mood and Admin edits were not viewed. Creating a workspace failed on the local database because only one non-chat model is configured there; the cause was not confirmed.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Sketchbook: two-way link with Notes, guide chat and tour
entries.goal: Let a sketch be put in a note and found again from either side, with buttons that show where things stand, and give Sketchbook the same help as Diagrams: a guide chat, a tour and tooltips.
entries.whatChanged: To Notes makes a new note with the picture inside it (shown in Preview) and a link back to the sketch, using the existing Notes routes. The note text is the record of the link, so nothing new is stored: GET /api/sketchbook/:id/notes finds the notes, and the list adds noteCount. The sketch button follows the state: To Notes when there is no note, Go to note when there is one, In N notes with a list when there are several, plus Put in another note once it is in a note. Each card in the collection shows In a note or In N notes. A deleted note or a removed link puts the button back to To Notes. Also the Sketchbook guide chat (POST /api/sketchbook-tutor, registered in guides.js, with a drift test against sketchbookTools.mjs), a 6-step tour with a Settings entry, and the (i) box text now comes from the same list as the guide. sketchNoteBody added to notePictures.mjs.
entries.benefit: A picture can be carried into a note and found again from either side without searching, and the buttons say what will happen before it is pressed. The same help as Diagrams is there for a first-time user.
entries.concerns: Checked on screen against a stand-in image service (draw, To Notes, Go to note, the note with the picture inside, the link back, the In a note card, the tour and the guide chat opening), not with the live image service. The guide chat was not sent a question: there is no AI key locally, so its answers are untested beyond the stand-in model test. The link relies on the note text containing the sketch link, so a person who edits the link out of the note loses the Go to note button (by design). A note keeps the picture it was given; later changes to the sketch are not copied. Opening the sketch from a note uses a normal link, which reloads the page. No package.json change.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Sketchbook: say plainly why a draw failed, and whether it was charged
entries.goal: A first live attempt failed with a message saying nothing was charged. That claim covered every failure, including one after the picture was drawn and paid for, and it hid the real reason (a 404 from the image service).
entries.whatChanged: Draw and Change now separate two failures. Image service failed: the message gives the likely reason (no FAL key, graphics model not usable, 404 meaning the model set in Settings is not a FAL model name, out of credit or locked, timeout, blocked) and says no spend was recorded. Picture came back but could not be saved: the message says the person may have been charged and to check Usage (feature graphics_sketchbook). Provider text is still logged and never shown. Tests cover each message.
entries.benefit: The person is told the real reason and is never told money was not spent when it may have been. The 404 case points at the Settings fix.
entries.concerns: The reason is picked by matching words in the provider error, so an unusual error still gets the generic line (plus "no spend recorded", which holds for any failure before a picture returns). The 404 wording is a best reading: the cause on the live site is not confirmed until the graphics model in Settings is checked. Does not fix the 404 itself; that is a Settings value.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Add Sketchbook: describe a scene, get a cartoon you can change later
entries.goal: Turn a described scene, theory or possibility into a cartoon, keep a collection of them, and let the person change the same picture later with more instructions, in pencil, coloured pens or coloured in. It is a separate tool from Graphics because it is project-shaped (saved collection, history, follow-up edits) while Graphics tools are one picture in, one picture out.
entries.whatChanged: New Sketchbook tool at /sketchbook and /sketchbook/:id (Content Creation). Describe a scene by typing or speaking, choose Pencil, Pen (7 ink colours) or Coloured in and a shape, and the image model draws it. Each sketch is saved; Change this picture changes the same sketch and keeps the last 6 earlier pictures with their look; Put back restores one (and the picture it replaced is kept); Colour it in redraws in colour; PNG, JPG, WebP and Copy picture. Collection with search, rename, copy and delete into the recycle bin with Undo. New table sketches, recycle bin adapter (type sketch), 11 API routes under /api/sketchbook behind the sketchbook flag (default off, preview), 11 route manifest entries. Reuses the Graphics image generation, paid-tool guard, daily cost cap (usage feature graphics_sketchbook) and content restrictions. New how-it-works box; docs/sketchbook.md and a key-files entry.
entries.benefit: Pictures of ideas and scenarios without drawing skill, kept in one private collection that can be reopened and refined, with no new image provider setup and the existing spending limits already applied.
entries.concerns: Not tried with the live image service: the screens and flow were checked in a browser against a stand-in that draws simple shapes, so how well the default FAL edit model (fal-ai/flux-kontext/dev, env SKETCHBOOK_EDIT_MODEL) follows instructions on cartoons, and its price (estimated 3 cents, env SKETCHBOOK_EDIT_COST_USD), are unproven. On a local copy a change can only nudge the picture (ComfyUI image to image). Each draw or change is a paid call and shares the daily image limit with Graphics. Switched off for members until an admin turns it on. Pictures are stored in the database (up to ~6 MB per sketch with its earlier pictures, 200 sketches per person). Not built: Copy to Notes, hand drawing, comic strips and consistent characters, guide chat and tour, SVG/PDF export. crossUser.test.js still fails on 11 older SERP Tracker routes missing from the manifest (not part of this commit). No package.json change, so the deploy should be fast.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Rename the Drawings tool to Diagrams (display names only)
entries.goal: The tool had become a flowcharting and diagramming tool (Draw it for me, loops, shape numbers, What have I missed?), so Drawings no longer described it.
entries.whatChanged: Renamed to Diagrams in everything a person sees: the menu and sidebar entry and page heading, the Feature Access label, the guide chat (Diagrams guide), the tour, help box and tooltips, New diagram / Your diagrams, the default title Untitled diagram, the recycle bin label, error messages, and the wording of notes made from it (From the diagram ...). Internal names are unchanged: the drawings feature flag, /drawings URL, /api/drawings routes, drawings table, customData keys, file names and the guide key. Notes still link back by their ](/drawings/N) link. The Ctrl+K aliases now include drawing, sketch, whiteboard and flowchart. docs/drawings.md and CLAUDE.md note the rename.
entries.benefit: The name says what the tool is for, and matches Excalidraw-style whiteboard users and flowchart users alike through the search aliases.
entries.concerns: Existing drawings keep their old default title (Untitled drawing) and existing notes keep From the drawing, since only new items use the new words. The rename was done with a script over the text people see; a first pass also changed SQL table names inside the code, which a test caught and was reverted before commit, and the remaining visible screens were checked for leftover words on the list page and editor only, not every message, guide answer or error. The board's own tooltips still say drawing (Excalidraw's text). The stored default title and the guide name change for everyone at once, including anyone who knew it as Drawings.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: remove duplicate Undo/Redo buttons from the board's top right
entries.goal: Remove a duplicate: the Undo and Redo buttons added in the board's top right only clicked the board's own arrows at its bottom left.
entries.whatChanged: Removed the Undo / Redo buttons from renderBoardTools, the canUndo / canRedo state and the 400 ms polling that kept them in step with the board. The board's own Undo / Redo arrows (bottom left) remain, and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z still work through handleKeyboardGlobally. Guide chat, tour and docs/drawings.md now point to the bottom-left arrows.
entries.benefit: One fewer duplicate control on a crowded screen, and no polling timer running while a drawing is open.
entries.concerns: The board's own Undo / Redo arrows are small. Checked on screen that one press removes a whole generated diagram and Redo then becomes available; the keyboard shortcuts were not exercised.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: move Undo/Redo, Keep shape/Free and Select all into the board
entries.goal: Declutter the bar above the drawing board by putting the board's own controls inside the drawing area.
entries.whatChanged: Undo / Redo, Keep shape / Free and Select all moved from the bar above the board into the board's top right, beside the Library button, using Excalidraw's renderTopRightUI (renderBoardTools in DrawingEditor.jsx). The bar above keeps Fit to screen, Snap to grid and Numbers. The board defines its own --color-primary and related variables inside itself, so Vault's values are read from the page root and set on the wrapper to keep the buttons in Vault's colours. Guide chat, tour and docs/drawings.md say where the controls now are.
entries.benefit: A shorter top bar, with the editing controls next to the tools they act on.
entries.concerns: Checked on screen at one screen width only. The wrapper has a maximum width and wraps, but on a narrow window the controls could crowd the board's own tool row. A stretch drag was not re-tested after the move (Keep shape state and Undo/Redo/Select all were). The Vault colours are read when the controls render, so a theme change shows after the next board redraw.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: shape numbers and "What have I missed?"
entries.goal: Let the owner refer to a shape by number when asking for changes on a busy drawing, and have the AI point out what a diagram may be missing.
entries.whatChanged: New Numbers button shows a small number on each box, diamond and oval that has writing in it. The number is saved in the box's customData.vaultNo and kept; the badges are an HTML overlay on the board, so they never print or export (PNG, SVG, file, Notes). New shapeNumbers.mjs: a box put in between two numbered boxes gets a sub-number of the one before (4.1, then 4.2); anything else gets the next whole number; a copied box with a repeated number gets its own. Numbers are given when the toggle is on, before Change it and What have I missed?, and for boxes the AI adds. The diagram JSON carries a num per node and the prompt tells the AI to copy every num and never invent one, so changes can refer to shapes (add a step after 7). New What have I missed? button in the Draw it for me box: POST /api/drawings/suggestions (askSuggestions in drawingDiagram.js, AI rate limit, usage feature drawing_diagram) sends only the diagram structure and returns up to six suggestions naming shapes by number; Add this makes the change through Change it, Dismiss hides one; nothing changes until Add this. Guide chat, help text, tour, tooltips, docs/drawings.md and routeManifest.json updated.
entries.benefit: On a drawing with many shapes a change or a gap can be pointed at by number, and the AI can raise gaps the owner had not thought of.
entries.concerns: Checked on screen only with a stand-in AI, never a real model: how useful and accurate the suggestions are, and whether a real model keeps shape numbers when changing a diagram, is unproven. The overlay badges are repositioned on every board change, which is fine for a few dozen shapes and unmeasured for hundreds. A number freed by deleting a shape is not reused within a visit, but after a drawing is reopened a freed top number can be reused. Only a box put in between two numbered boxes gets a sub-number; branches and additions at either end take whole numbers. Each What have I missed? press is one AI request. Separately, crossUser.test.js reports 11 SERP Tracker routes missing from routeManifest.json; those are not Drawings routes and were not changed here.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: change any diagram by voice, waiting steps loop back
entries.goal: Let the owner change an existing drawing by voice (insert, add at the start or end), not only the diagram the AI drew a moment ago, and make waiting steps (a deposit not paid) loop back to the earlier step dependably.
entries.whatChanged: New client/src/pages/drawings/sceneDiagram.mjs (readDiagram) reads a diagram back out of the drawing: boxes with bound writing (rectangle = box, diamond = decision, ellipse = start/end) and arrows bound at both ends, with labels and two-way heads. Change it now uses that instead of the structure remembered from the last AI run, so it works on hand-made diagrams and ones from earlier visits, and reflects hand edits; the diagram containing the selection is used, otherwise the biggest, over 40 boxes is refused. The pieces read are deleted and the updated diagram drawn at their top left (one Undo reverts). The Change it box shows whenever a diagram is readable; Start fresh was removed. The AI prompt now describes insert / add at start / add at end / rename / remove / loop back, and says a step that must wait (payment, approval, reply) is a Yes/No decision whose No arrow loops back to the earlier step. Guide chat, help text and docs/drawings.md updated.
entries.benefit: Diagrams can be extended or corrected by voice at any time, including older and hand-made ones, and processes that must wait for something loop back instead of moving on.
entries.concerns: Seen working on screen only with a stand-in AI (reload, then add a step after the visit); never with a real model, so how well the model inserts steps or draws the deposit loop from real wording is unproven. Boxes moved by hand inside the diagram are laid out again on a change. Arrows from outside a replaced diagram that were bound to its boxes become unattached. Reading a diagram relies on writing being bound inside boxes (the board's normal behaviour), so loose text next to a box is not read. Several diagrams on one drawing rely on selecting a box to choose; otherwise the biggest is used.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: tidy top row (Draw it for me to More tools, one Notes button, Select all, Fit to screen)
entries.goal: Declutter the Drawings top row, and add the Select all and Fit to screen controls the owner asked for.
entries.whatChanged: Draw it for me left the top row and is now an item in the board's own More tools menu (Generate section, AI tag), added with Excalidraw's TTDDialogTrigger child component; when the board opens its built-in text-to-diagram dialog for that item, onChange closes it at once and opens the existing Draw it for me panel. To Notes and In a note are merged into one button: To Notes when the drawing is in no note; otherwise In a note / In N notes opening a list of Go to each note plus Put in another note. The Two-way arrow button was removed (the board's Arrowheads panel sets both ends). New Select all (selects every live element) and Fit to screen (scrollToContent fitToViewport, zooms in or out) buttons. Guide chat catalog, help text, tour and docs/drawings.md updated.
entries.benefit: A shorter, less congested top row, one notes button instead of two, and easier resizing of whole drawings.
entries.concerns: The More tools entry relies on Excalidraw's TTDDialogTrigger and on its dialog state names (openDialog ttd, tab text-to-diagram); an Excalidraw upgrade could break it, in which case the board's own dialog would show instead. Checked on screen that the item appears, opens our panel and the board dialog does not show. The To Notes to In a note swap after saving a note was not re-run on screen after the merge. Select all and Fit to screen were seen working; the final fit margin (85%) was set after the check and not looked at.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: undo/redo, keep shape, two-way arrows, loop routing, snap to grid
entries.goal: Act on the owner's feedback after first real use of Draw it for me: stretch everything without bending it, two-way arrows, loops in decision flows, snap to grid, and a multi-step undo/redo.
entries.whatChanged: Undo and Redo buttons above the board drive the board's own unlimited history (a whole generated diagram is one step); Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z work anywhere on the page. Keep shape / Free (remembered) decides whether dragging a corner keeps proportions, with a real Shift doing the opposite for one drag, by overriding the shift state on pointer events during a stretch. Two-way arrow button for selected arrows; Draw it for me may now return two-way edges and merges an arrow each way between two boxes into one. Loop arrows are routed round the outside of the diagram with sharp corners, leaving from underneath when a box sits beside the source, never crossing a box; decision diamonds are larger so text stays on one line. Snap to grid toggles the board's grid, saved with the drawing. Guide chat catalog, help text, tour, tooltips and docs/drawings.md updated.
entries.benefit: Diagrams can be resized, edited and corrected without redrawing; loops and two-way relationships read clearly; boxes line up; mistakes are easy to step back from.
entries.concerns: Tested on screen only with a stand-in AI, never a real model. Keep shape relies on overriding event.shiftKey, which depends on Excalidraw internals and may need rework when the library is upgraded; verified with Select all on a drag-box selection, not on single boxes or pictures. Snap to grid was confirmed by button state and saved setting, not by dragging a box. Ctrl+Z shortcuts were not exercised; only the buttons were. Undo history is per visit and is not saved. Undo/Redo buttons read the board's own button state every 400 ms.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: Draw it for me (dictate or type a scenario, the AI develops a diagram)
entries.goal: Let a person dictate (or type) a scenario and have a diagram developed from it, instead of drawing every box and arrow by hand.
entries.whatChanged: New Draw it for me button above the drawing board. A panel takes a scenario said into the microphone or typed (the shared dictation text box), and Draw it adds the diagram to the open drawing as ordinary Excalidraw pieces, below anything already there (top left of the screen on an empty drawing), in the look the drawing is in; the panel closes and the board zooms to fit without zooming a small diagram in; one press of the board's Undo removes the whole diagram. A Change it box (say what to change) redraws the last diagram in the same place, replacing the pieces it made earlier (found by a run tag in their customData) and leaving anything drawn by hand around it; Start fresh forgets it; the diagram to change is kept for the visit only. New route POST /api/drawings/diagram (behind the AI rate limit and the drawings flag): one call on the workspace standard model asks for ONLY a structure (kind flow / org / mind map / timeline / relationship, direction, boxes with a short label and shape box / decision / start-end, and arrows with optional labels), never positions. The reply is untrusted and is checked and cleaned (safe unique ids, short labels, known shapes, arrows only between boxes that exist, up to 40 boxes and 80 arrows; unusable replies give a plain message, never raw model text); the person's words are fenced so they cannot pass for instructions. Only the words typed or said are sent, never any drawing; usage is logged as drawing_diagram. The layout is ours (layers by longest path, loops tolerated, boxes sized to wrapped labels, arrows bound to box edges) and goes through Excalidraw's convertToExcalidrawElements. Guide, help box, tour, tooltips, key-files and docs/drawings.md updated. No new package.
filesImpacted: server/services/drawingDiagram.js (new: prompt, checking, ask) and drawingDiagram.test.js
client/src/pages/drawings/DrawingEditor.jsx (button, panel, placing and replacing a diagram)
client/src/pages/drawings/drawingsTools.mjs, server/services/drawingsTutor.js and its test, client/src/utils/tours/drawingsTour.js (guide, help, tour)
entries.benefit: A scenario said or typed becomes a tidy editable diagram in seconds, in the person's own look, and it can be adjusted by saying what to change.
entries.concerns: NOT TRIED WITH A REAL MODEL: there is no AI key locally, so the screen was checked with a stand-in that returns fixed diagrams (a flow with a decision, an org chart, a change that adds a box), including the Clean look, a reload and Undo. How good the boxes are from real descriptions, how long a call takes, and whether the 4,000-character and 40-box limits suit real use are unknown. Dictation by microphone was not tried (typing was). Costs one AI request per Draw it or Change it (logged in Usage as drawing_diagram), behind the existing AI rate limit. Flows, org charts, mind maps, timelines and relationship diagrams only: not drawings to scale (floor plans), illustrations, or reading or tidying a drawing the person made. A change replaces the last diagram including any hand edits to it, and cannot be made after the drawing has been closed. The keyboard Ctrl+Z sent by the browser-automation tool did not reach the board while the on-screen Undo button worked (probably the tool, not the app; not proven). Not run on Railway. No package change, so a normal fast deploy.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: In a note button on each card in the list
entries.goal: Show on the list of drawings which drawings are in notes, as the drawing editor already does, so the way back to a note does not need the drawing to be opened first.
entries.whatChanged: Each card in Your drawings now shows an In a note button (In N notes when there are several) when notes link back to that drawing; a drawing in no note shows nothing. One note goes straight to it; several open a short list of titles under the card's buttons (fetched when clicked). GET /api/drawings now adds noteCount to every row, worked out in ONE query over the person's notes that mention "/drawings/" (regexp_matches on the "](/drawings/N)" links), not one search per drawing; a note that links twice counts once, and another person's notes never count. Guide wording, help text and docs updated; tests cover the counts (including 7 versus 70 and another person).
filesImpacted: client/src/pages/drawings/DrawingsList.jsx (the button and list on each card)
entries.benefit: From the list you can see at a glance which drawings are in notes and jump to the note with one click.
entries.concerns: The note count is found from the link text in each note, so a note whose link was edited out, or that was deleted, stops counting; a note that merely holds the same Markdown link counts. One pattern-match query runs over the person's notes every time the list opens: fine at normal note counts, not measured on a very large notes table. Tried on screen locally with drawings in no note, one note and two notes (the one-note and two-note paths both opened the right note); not tried on Railway. No package change, so a normal fast deploy.

entries.author: mrb
entries.subject: Drawings: In a note button (go from a drawing to the notes it was sent to)
